sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: How can you measure your actual visual-lead seconds while rolling down a road?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: To measure the visual lead, time travel from the current position to a fixed object ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Roughly how many seconds and feet does reacting and stopping from sixty miles per hour take on good pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: The guide estimates that reacting and stopping at sixty miles per hour can require about four to five seconds or three hundred fifty-nine feet under good conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Under good conditions, about how many seconds and feet does reacting and stopping take at thirty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: The guide estimates about two to three seconds or one hundred twenty-three feet for reacting and stopping at thirty miles per hour under good conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What safety requirement links how far ahead you can see with how fast you may travel?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Visibility must provide enough distance to stop before an obstacle in the travel path.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Beyond marked street corners, what everyday entrances count as intersections because traffic streams cross or merge?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: An intersection includes a place where traffic streams cross or merge, including driveways and parking-lot entrances.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Approaching an intersection, which six elements does Louisiana's guide tell you to scan?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Approaching a junction, check cross traffic, approaching vehicles, pedestrians, controls, visibility and the road surface.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: After halting at an intersection, in what exact order should you turn your head before pulling out?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: After stopping at an intersection, look left, then right, then left again before proceeding.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: Should you stop scanning cross streets just because cross traffic faces a red light or stop sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Continue checking for crossing traffic even when other drivers face a stop sign or red light.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What exit condition on the far side of an intersection must exist before you roll past the stop line?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Enter an intersection only with a clear path through it so a later stop will not block the crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What scanning habit do busy sidewalks, schools, playgrounds, and parking lots demand?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Busy sidewalks, playgrounds, school grounds and parking areas call for extra side-to-side scanning.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which two oncoming traffic movements outrank a driver waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: A left-turning driver must yield to approaching vehicles traveling straight or turning right.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What destination check prevents getting stranded broadside across oncoming lanes during a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Before completing a left turn, make sure vehicles or pedestrians will not trap the turning vehicle in opposing traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which three conflict sources must you scan before turning right at an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Before a right turn, check traffic approaching from the left, opposing left-turners and crossing pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: What speed and visual routine applies whenever you approach a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Slow on a railroad approach and check both track directions for trains or maintenance equipment.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Before which four driving situations does Louisiana's guide emphasize checking traffic behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Check rear traffic before changing lanes, slowing, entering from the roadside or descending a long hill.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What two rear hazards should your mirrors clear before you start changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Before a lane change, check mirrors for vehicles in the destination lane or about to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: How does the Louisiana guide define a vehicle's blind spots?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: A blind spot is an area around the vehicle that the mirrors do not show.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What physical check clears your blind spot right before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Check the blind spot by looking over the shoulder toward the intended lane change.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What forward mistake must you avoid while checking mirrors or glancing over your shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Do not look away from the forward path for too long while checking behind or beside the vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How many seconds of open traffic gap does Louisiana's guide recommend finding before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: The guide recommends identifying a four-to-five-second traffic gap before a lane change.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: In order, what five steps complete a clean, legal lane change from blinker on to blinker off?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Signal, check the intended lane again, adjust speed, enter it safely and cancel the signal after changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: When is checking your mirrors while braking especially critical to prevent a rear-end hit?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Check mirrors while slowing, particularly at an unexpected turn into a driveway or parking space.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: Why should you monitor your mirrors closely while descending a long downhill grade?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: On a long downhill grade, watch behind for large vehicles approaching rapidly.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: How should your inside rearview mirror be aimed before you put the car in gear?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Adjust the interior rear-view mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: How should outside side-mirror views relate to your inside rearview mirror's coverage?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: The guide describes positioning side-mirror views to overlap the interior mirror’s rearward view.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What slice of forward travel counts as perception distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Perception distance is the distance traveled between seeing a hazard and recognizing it.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Which span of travel defines reaction distance during an emergency stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Reaction distance is the distance traveled after recognizing danger and before physically applying the brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: What happens during the braking-distance portion of a stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: Braking distance is the travel that occurs while the brakes are being applied.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: Which three distances add together to equal total stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: Total stopping distance includes perception, reaction and braking distances.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: Besides driver response speed, what four physical factors change how much road you need to stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: Actual stopping needs vary with response time, road and weather conditions, vehicle weight, brakes and tires.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: What two dangerous outcomes climb sharply as vehicle speed rises?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: Higher speed increases braking distance and the potential severity of a crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: At what exact moment do you begin counting your three-second following check?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: The guide’s three-second following check starts when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed roadside object.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: What does reaching that roadside marker before finishing a three-second count tell you?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: If the following vehicle reaches that object before three seconds have elapsed, the gap is too short under the guide’s basic rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: What should you do right after timing less than three seconds behind the car ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: Increase the gap and repeat the timing check until the basic following interval is met.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: To how many seconds does Louisiana's guide expand your basic following interval on wet roads or in bad weather?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: The guide recommends expanding the basic following interval to four seconds in poor weather or on wet pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How should you respond when another driver merges into your open following cushion?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: When a vehicle enters the following gap, fall back to restore safe space.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Why must your following gap grow wider whenever pavement turns slick?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Leave more space on slippery roads because the vehicle needs farther to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: What specific hazard explains leaving extra following room behind a motorcycle?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.memory_hook: Extra room in case rider falls
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Provide extra following room behind a motorcycle because the rider might fall.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: For what two visibility reasons must you hang farther back behind a bus or box truck?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Leave added room behind a large vehicle that hides the road ahead or whose driver may not see a vehicle close behind.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does hitching a trailer behind your vehicle change stopping physics?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Towing a trailer adds combined weight and increases stopping distance.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How should darkness or poor visibility change the space you hold behind traffic ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Poor visibility and darkness call for additional following space.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: Why must you hold extra distance behind fire trucks, ambulances, or patrol units?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Leave extra space behind emergency vehicles so they have room to operate.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Which two vehicle classes should you expect to halt at railroad crossings—and trail with extra space?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Expect some buses and hazardous-material vehicles to stop at railroad tracks and leave additional room behind them.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Why should you leave extra bumper gap when halted behind another vehicle on an uphill incline?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: When stopped on an incline, allow for the possibility that the vehicle ahead may roll backward as it starts.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Instead of wrestling a tight turnaround on a busy street, what route choice does the guide prefer?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Going around the block is preferable to turning around on a busy street.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Under what exact road conditions does Louisiana's guide allow a three-point turnabout?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: The guide limits a three-point turnabout to a two-lane roadway where a U-turn will not fit and going around the block is unavailable.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Should you set the parking brake only on hills, or on flat ground as well?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: The guide recommends applying the parking brake whenever parking, on level ground as well as on hills.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: In an automatic-transmission car, does setting the parking brake replace shifting into park?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: In an automatic vehicle, the parking brake supplements rather than replaces selecting park.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: In what foot-and-lever order should you secure an automatic car when parking?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: The guide recommends setting the parking brake with the service brake still depressed before selecting park.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: What brake step must happen before you pull out of a parking spot?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Release the parking brake before driving away.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: Which way must your front tires point when parking downhill next to a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: When parking downhill beside a curb, point the front wheels toward the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: Which way must your front tires point when parking uphill beside a raised curb?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: When parking uphill beside a curb, point the front wheels away from the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: With no curb present, which way should your parked wheels turn whether facing uphill or downhill?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: Without a curb, turn the wheels toward the road edge whether the parked vehicle faces uphill or downhill.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: Along with turned wheels, what two mechanical settings keep a hill-parked vehicle out of traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Use the parking brake and an appropriate parked gear so the vehicle does not roll into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: What four-part routine guides you smoothly into an angled parking stall?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: When entering an angled parking space, check traffic, signal, slow and leave room for nearby vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: What all-around scan is mandatory before backing out of any parking stall?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: Before reversing from a parking space, check for obstructions and traffic in every direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: Why must you inch out at creeping speed when backing from between two parked vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: Move slowly when reversing from between parked vehicles because the view of approaching traffic is limited.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: Which direction does your front bumper swing while steering through a reverse turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: During a reversing turn, the vehicle’s front end swings opposite the direction in which the rear is turning.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: Which two ways of entering a perpendicular parking stall does Louisiana's guide prefer when possible?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: The guide prefers backing into or pulling through a perpendicular parking space when possible.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.front: Unless stall lines mark otherwise, at least how many feet should remain between parallel-parked bumpers?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.expected_back: The guide’s parallel-parking instructions leave at least two feet between bumpers and adjacent vehicles unless markings indicate otherwise.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.front: Which four visual clues warn that a curb-parked car is about to pull into your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.expected_back: Brake lights, reverse lights, a signal or outward-turned front wheels can warn that a parked vehicle is about to move.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.front: What three sudden hazards should you anticipate while driving beside a row of parked cars?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.expected_back: Watch for a door opening and for people or bicycles emerging between parked vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.front: Within how many inches of the right-hand curb must your right wheels rest when parallel parked?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.expected_back: The guide requires right-side wheels to be within eighteen inches of the right curb when parallel parked.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.front: What four security and safety steps are required before walking away from an unattended parked vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.memory_hook: Engine off, key out, lock, brake
sec08-card-sec08-R30.expected_back: Before leaving a parked vehicle unattended, shut off the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition and set the brake.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.front: What must you check for before swinging open a traffic-side door?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.expected_back: Before opening a street-side door, check for passing vehicles and bicycles.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.front: Which four everyday travel paths may you never block by parking?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.expected_back: Do not park on a sidewalk, across a driveway, within an intersection or in a bicycle lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.front: How many feet must you stay clear when parking near a fire hydrant versus a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.expected_back: The guide prohibits parking within fifteen feet of a hydrant or fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.front: Parking is banned within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.expected_back: The guide prohibits parking within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-R35.front: How far from a fire-station driveway is parking banned on the same side versus across the street?
sec08-card-sec08-R35.expected_back: The guide prohibits parking within twenty feet of a fire-station driveway on its side of the street or seventy-five feet on the opposite side.

sec08-card-sec08-R36.front: Along with double-parking beside another car, which three highway structures ban parking altogether?
sec08-card-sec08-R36.expected_back: Double parking and parking on bridges, overpasses or inside tunnels are prohibited in the guide.

sec08-card-sec08-R37.front: What two posted or active work-area rules bar parking on otherwise open curb space?
sec08-card-sec08-R37.expected_back: Do not park where official signs prohibit it or where the vehicle would obstruct a construction area.

sec08-card-sec08-R38.front: Within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or roadside traffic signal is parking prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-R38.expected_back: The guide prohibits parking within twenty feet of a roadside signal, stop sign or yield sign.

sec08-card-sec08-R39.front: How do white-painted curbs differ from yellow-painted curbs under Louisiana's guide?
sec08-card-sec08-R39.expected_back: A white curb denotes short stops; yellow denotes loading or another restriction.

sec08-card-sec08-R40.front: What restrictions do red curb paint and blue curb paint signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R40.expected_back: Red curb paint indicates fire-related restrictions, and blue identifies an accessibility restriction.

sec08-card-sec08-R41.front: What purpose does the striped access aisle next to an accessible parking stall serve?
sec08-card-sec08-R41.expected_back: An access aisle beside accessible parking provides space for loading equipment and entering or leaving the vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R42.front: Even for a one-minute errand, what is required to use an accessible parking space legally?
sec08-card-sec08-R42.expected_back: Use an accessible parking space only with the required authorization.

sec08-card-sec08-R43.front: May shoppers leave shopping carts or park a narrow motorcycle inside a striped access aisle?
sec08-card-sec08-R43.expected_back: Do not block the intended use of an access aisle, including by leaving a cart or motorcycle in it.

sec08-card-sec08-R44.front: What immediate consequence can hit a vehicle parked illegally in an accessible stall or access aisle?
sec08-card-sec08-R44.expected_back: Unauthorized use of accessible parking or its access aisle can result in towing and related costs.

sec08-card-sec08-R45.front: What must a left-side pass never force either oncoming traffic or the overtaken driver to do?
sec08-card-sec08-R45.expected_back: A left-side pass must not force an approaching driver or the passed driver to slow or leave the road.

sec08-card-sec08-R46.front: Before closing within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you finish passing and return right?
sec08-card-sec08-R46.expected_back: The guide requires completing a pass before coming within one hundred feet of an opposing vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R47.front: Which three sightline, paint, or surface conditions forbid passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R47.expected_back: Do not pass with a view blocked by a hill or bend, across a solid yellow line on the driver’s side, or on the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-R48.front: Passing is barred within one hundred feet of which four roadway features?
sec08-card-sec08-R48.expected_back: The guide bars passing within one hundred feet of a junction, railroad crossing, bridge or tunnel.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: Which two official ownership and road-use records does Louisiana require for a motor vehicle?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: Louisiana requires a motor vehicle to have a title and registration.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: At which two types of offices can you apply for a Louisiana title, registration, and license plate?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: Title, registration and plate applications can be handled through a motor vehicle office or licensed public tag agent.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: How can the cost of using a licensed public tag agent differ from visiting an OMV office?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: A public tag agent may charge additional service fees.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: Which two origin and sale documents does a Louisiana new-car dealer provide?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: A Louisiana new-vehicle dealer supplies an assigned certificate of origin and a notarized invoice.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: How do dealerships usually handle sales taxes, fees, and filing for your title and plate?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: The guide says dealers commonly collect taxes and fees and send the documents for the buyer’s title and plate.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: How must a temporary dealer license plate be mounted or displayed on your car?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: A temporary dealer plate must be visible from behind the vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: What must the prior owner or used-car dealer do with the certificate of title when selling?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: For a used-vehicle purchase, the previous owner or dealer must properly assign the certificate of title to the buyer.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: When must the seller hand over the properly assigned title on a vehicle sale?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: The seller must deliver the properly assigned title when the vehicle is sold or delivered.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: If a used vehicle's title shows an existing lien, what must you verify before buying?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: If a title lists a lien, check for release by an authorized representative of the lienholder.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: Which notarized ownership paper and coverage statement appear on the guide's title-application list?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: The guide’s title application list includes the assigned notarized title and a liability-insurance declaration.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: When can you skip bringing a separate bill of sale during a Louisiana title transfer?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: A separate bill of sale is unnecessary under the guide when the selling price is entered in the title’s designated space.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: What extra document must accompany your title application if you financed the vehicle with a loan?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: A mortgage document is required with the title application when applicable.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: Where must you keep your vehicle's registration certificate, and when must you produce it?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: Keep the registration certificate inside the vehicle and show it when law enforcement requests it.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: Where can you get a duplicate registration certificate if your original goes missing?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: A duplicate registration can be obtained through a motor vehicle office or public tag agent if the original is lost.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: What must a new Louisiana resident do for vehicles brought along from another state?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: A new Louisiana resident must transfer title and registration for vehicles brought into the state during the move.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: Which three out-of-state and coverage records start a new resident's Louisiana vehicle registration?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.expected_back: A new resident’s registration documents include the out-of-state title and registration and evidence of insurance.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: What does Louisiana accept when an out-of-state bank or lienholder is still holding your physical title?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: When an out-of-state lienholder holds the title, the guide calls for a photocopy of it.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: Why should a new resident bring proof of vehicle taxes already paid in the previous state?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: Bring proof of taxes paid in the previous state when transferring a vehicle to Louisiana.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: Within how many days after moving must you update the address on your vehicle registration?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: Correct the address on a vehicle registration within ten days after moving.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: What practical headache comes from leaving an old address on your vehicle registration?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: An incorrect registration address can prevent delivery of renewal information.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: What financial-responsibility proof is required to obtain a Louisiana license plate?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: A plate applicant needs evidence of required liability coverage or an allowed substitute.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: What two ongoing duties apply to insurance proof whenever a vehicle is driven?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: Maintain insurance evidence in an operating vehicle and provide it when an officer requests it.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: What two immediate enforcement actions can hit your car if you cannot show proof of insurance?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: The guide warns that inability to provide insurance proof can result in plate seizure and possible impoundment.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: What two penalties threaten someone who submits or shows false insurance information?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: Providing false insurance information can result in registration suspension and court penalties.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: Before dropping insurance on a car you are taking off the road, what must you turn in to OMV?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Before canceling insurance on a vehicle that will no longer be used on the highway, the guide directs surrendering its plate to OMV.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: What two date details printed on your registration certificate show when your plate expires?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: The registration certificate states the month and year in which the plate expires.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: To what address does the motor vehicle agency send a registration renewal invitation?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: A registration renewal invitation is sent to the last address recorded with the agency.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: Which two remote channels can eligible vehicle owners use by following their renewal invitation?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: Eligible owners can follow the renewal invitation’s instructions for online or telephone renewal.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: Whom must you notify if your registration renewal notice shows an error or outdated address?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Report renewal-application errors or address changes to the motor vehicle agency.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: Does never receiving a mailed renewal reminder excuse driving on expired registration?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: Receiving a renewal reminder is a courtesy; the owner remains responsible for valid registration.

sec17-card-sec17-R13.front: What sign color and wording identify an authorized Louisiana motor vehicle inspection station?
sec17-card-sec17-R13.expected_back: The guide identifies authorized inspection stations by an orange sign naming the Louisiana motor vehicle inspection station.

sec17-card-sec17-R14.front: Which three Louisiana municipalities run their own separate vehicle inspection programs?
sec17-card-sec17-R14.expected_back: The guide describes separate municipal inspection programs for New Orleans, Kenner and Westwego.

sec17-card-sec17-R15.front: Where should you check exact fees for commercial rigs, motorcycles, specialty plates, or plate transfers?
sec17-card-sec17-R15.expected_back: Contact your local Office of Motor Vehicles or visit its website for specific commercial vehicle, motorcycle, special plate and plate transfer fees.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: What right do bicyclists hold on Louisiana public roads, and what legal duty comes with it?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Bicyclists have a right to use public roads and must follow applicable traffic laws.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How must motorists treat a bicyclist when yielding right-of-way at an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Yield to a bicyclist at an intersection as required for other roadway users.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Which surface conditions allow a bicyclist to move away from the roadway's right edge?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: A bicyclist may move away from the right edge to avoid debris, damaged pavement or other hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Where on the roadway may a bicyclist position when getting ready to make a left turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A bicyclist may move toward a left-turn lane when preparing to turn left.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: On a two-way street with oncoming traffic approaching, how must you handle passing a bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: On a two-way road, do not squeeze between an oncoming vehicle and a bicycle; wait for opposing traffic to clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: At least how many feet of clearance must a passing motorist leave beside a slower bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: The guide requires at least three feet between a passing motor vehicle and a slower bicycle.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Why must you leave extra lateral space when a bicyclist rides alongside parked cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Give a bicyclist room to avoid doors opening from parked vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: How should you adjust your clearance around a bicycle when your vehicle is towing a trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Allow additional passing room when towing a trailer near a bicycle.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: How do wind, rain, or ice affect a bicyclist, and what two adjustments should motorists make?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Wind, rain or ice can make a bicyclist less stable, so reduce speed and leave extra space.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What must you do before turning left when a bicyclist is approaching from the opposite direction?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Before turning left, wait for an opposing bicyclist to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Why must you never overtake a bicyclist and then immediately turn right?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Do not overtake a bicycle and immediately turn right across its path.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What check is required before swinging your parked vehicle's door open toward a travel lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Before opening a door toward traffic, look for an approaching bicycle.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: What sudden move should you anticipate when a bicyclist approaches railroad tracks or a metal grate?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: A bicycle may slow or change position when crossing tracks or a metal grate.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Why do children riding bicycles demand extra caution from nearby motorists?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Children on bicycles may change direction unexpectedly and may not know the traffic rules.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Under Louisiana's guide, which young cyclists must wear an approved, fitted, and fastened helmet?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: The guide advises helmet use and states that children younger than twelve must wear an approved, properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: How should bicyclists communicate maneuvers to traffic, and how must they treat signs and signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Bicyclists should communicate with hand signals and follow traffic signs and signals.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Where does a bicyclist normally ride relative to traffic flow, and when may the rider use the lane center?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: A bicyclist normally rides with traffic on the roadway’s right side but may use the lane center to avoid a hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Who holds priority when a bicyclist encounters pedestrians in a crosswalk or on a sidewalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians at crosswalks and on sidewalks.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Which front and rear visibility equipment does the guide require on a bicycle ridden at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: The guide requires a white forward bicycle lamp and a rear-facing red lamp or reflector for night riding.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: How many riders may a bicycle legally carry on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A bicycle must not carry more people than it is designed and equipped to carry.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Why do motorists often misjudge an approaching motorcycle's distance and closing speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: A motorcycle’s narrow profile can make its speed and distance difficult for a motorist to judge.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Why can a fast mirror check miss a nearby motorcycle completely?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: A motorcycle can be missed in a quick glance or hidden in another vehicle’s blind spot.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: For what three safety reasons might a motorcyclist shift left or right inside a single lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: A motorcycle rider may change position within the lane to see better, be visible or avoid a hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: How do wind gusts, pavement defects, and track surfaces hit a motorcycle compared with a car?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Road defects, wind and track surfaces that seem minor to a car can seriously affect a motorcycle.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car share that lane beside it?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to the full lane; a motorist must not crowd into that lane beside it.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: How should you execute a pass around a motorcycle compared with passing another car?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Pass a motorcycle as a full vehicle, leaving room rather than passing closely within its lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Why is it risky to pull out solely because an approaching motorcycle's turn signal is flashing?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Do not assume a motorcycle will turn solely because its signal is on; some signals do not cancel automatically.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: When is it safe to pull across an approaching motorcycle's path at an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Wait until the motorcycle’s maneuver is clear before moving across its path.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: At least how many seconds of following distance does Louisiana's guide call for behind a motorcycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: The guide calls for at least four seconds of following room behind a motorcycle and more when conditions require it.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: How should you manage high-beam headlights when meeting or following a motorcycle at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Dim headlights for a motorcycle just as for another vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How do a large truck's stopping and maneuvering space needs compare with a passenger car's?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Large trucks need more room to stop and maneuver than passenger vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Why must you avoid darting into the open gap left directly in front of a moving truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Do not cut into the open space in front of a truck because that space is needed for stopping.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: What happens to visibility when a small car sits tight against the nose of a long-hooded truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: A vehicle very close in front of a long-hooded truck may be hidden from its driver.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What rule applies to lingering alongside a large truck inside its side blind zone?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Do not remain alongside a truck in its blind spot.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: What warning applies whenever you cannot see the truck driver's face in the rig's mirror?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: If the truck driver’s face cannot be seen in a mirror, the guide warns that the driver may not see the nearby vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What adjustment must you make if you follow a truck so closely that its side mirrors disappear?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: If following so closely that the truck’s side mirrors cannot be seen, increase the gap.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Why must you give a turning semi-truck extra clearance throughout its corner?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Give a turning truck ample room because its blind spots and the relationship of cab and trailer change during the turn.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Why should you stop farther back behind a heavy truck waiting on an uphill grade?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Leave extra room behind a truck stopped on an incline in case it rolls backward when starting.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Why should you minimize time spent next to a large truck in windy weather?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Avoid staying beside a truck longer than necessary during windy weather.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: How should you hold the steering wheel while passing a large truck, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Maintain firm control of the wheel when passing a truck because air turbulence can affect the smaller vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Which three everyday highway actions take a large truck noticeably longer than a passenger car?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: A large truck generally takes longer than a car to accelerate, stop or be passed.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: In good weather and dry pavement, how many seconds should you keep behind a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: In good conditions, the guide recommends a four-to-five-second following interval behind a truck.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: How must your following gap behind a truck change when weather or pavement turns poor?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Leave an even longer gap behind a truck in poor weather or road conditions.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: What two visibility advantages do you gain by trailing farther behind a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Following farther behind a truck improves the view ahead and reduces exposure to wheel spray.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: Which headlight setting belongs on when following a truck at night, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Keep low beams on when following a truck at night because bright beams reflect from its mirrors toward the driver.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: What do truck mudguards cut down on, and what wet-weather hazard do they fail to stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Mudguards reduce debris but do not eliminate water spray from a truck’s wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: Which two vehicle items must stay in top shape when sharing rainy roads with trucks?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: Maintain clean glass and effective wipers when traveling near trucks in rain.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: What should you do right before meeting an oncoming truck in the rain?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: Prepare the wipers before an oncoming truck passes in rain so spray is cleared promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: What visibility condition must be met before you pull out to pass a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Do not start passing a truck unless the road ahead can be seen clearly.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: How do you lessen the blinding effect of wheel spray thrown off a nearby truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: Increase separation from a truck to reduce the effect of its spray on visibility.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: Around which four sides of a large truck do No-Zones hide nearby vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Truck no-zones are areas at the front, rear and sides where nearby vehicles can be hidden from the driver.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: On which side does Louisiana's guide direct motorists to pass a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: The guide directs motorists to pass a truck on its left.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: After passing a semi-truck, what must show in your rearview mirror before pulling back ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Before returning in front after passing a truck, wait until the whole truck front is visible in the rear-view mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.front: Why should highway drivers give an entering semi-truck generous room to merge?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.expected_back: Allow a truck room to merge, remembering that it needs longer to reach highway speed.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.front: Why is watching a large vehicle's turn signal critical when it moves slightly left near an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.expected_back: Watch a large vehicle’s turn signal because a right turn may start with a swing toward the left.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.front: Where must you never position your car when a truck or bus is making a right turn?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.expected_back: Never drive between a right-turning truck or bus and the curb.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.front: When may you start turning at an intersection next to a turning truck or bus?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.expected_back: Wait for a truck or bus to finish turning before attempting to turn beside it.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What connected network makes up the Highway Transportation System?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Every neighborhood street, parish lane, and interstate links into one shared public-and-private traffic web.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: How does the Highway Transportation System aim to move people and goods—and what else does it protect?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Moving travelers and freight smoothly only succeeds when safety and environmental protection stay balanced.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Who holds responsibility for obeying Highway Transportation System rules and cooperating on the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Traffic stays predictable only when drivers, cyclists, and walkers all cooperate under shared rules.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which three everyday, commercial, and urgent trip types rely on the road network?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: The exact same asphalt carries morning commuters, grocery freight, and responding ambulances.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Beyond drivers, passengers, and walkers, which four roadside or neighborhood groups belong to the system's people component?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Counting road crews, officers, medics, and kids playing near curbs keeps your scan wider than bumpers.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: What wide range of vehicles shares the Highway Transportation System alongside passenger cars?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Sharing lanes safely means expecting nimble bicycles, slow tractors, heavy semis, and urgent fire rigs.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which route systems and specialty highways make up the system's roads component?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Knowing which route system you are on helps anticipate speed, access ramps, and intersections.
sec03-card-sec03-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Interstate, U.S., state, county, toll, parkways

visual_sync.text_span: Interstate, U.S., state, county, toll, parkways

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Which five daily personal activities does the road network make possible?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Almost every routine errand—commuting, classes, groceries, and weekend trips—depends on connected streets.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Which five major industries and economic activities depend directly on the highway network?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Building cars, paving roads, hauling goods, tourism, and repair shops all run on highway access.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Besides driver licensing, which four vehicle records and payments does Louisiana's OMV manage?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: OMV connects qualified drivers across Louisiana with properly titled, registered, and plated motor vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: How do city police, state highway patrol, and parish sheriff's deputies support safe travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Visible traffic enforcement deters speeding, impairment, and reckless moves across local and state roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: How do traffic courts fit into keeping roadways safe?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Roadside citations only carry weight because courts adjudicate charges and uphold penalties fairly.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: Contrast what highway engineering improves against what vehicle engineering improves?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Safer interchanges come from highway engineers, while airbags, crumple zones, and brakes come from vehicle engineers.
sec03-card-sec03-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Highway upgrades roads; vehicle upgrades cars

visual_sync.text_span: Highway upgrades roads; vehicle upgrades cars

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: How do emergency responders and trauma centers reduce losses from highway collisions?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Rapid roadside stabilization and hospital trauma care turn otherwise fatal injuries into recoveries.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Which three qualities does public traffic education build in road users?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Knowing the law and steering smoothly still fail without a cooperative, safety-first mindset.
sec03-card-sec03-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Rule knowledge, driving skills, safe attitudes

visual_sync.text_span: Rule knowledge, driving skills, safe attitudes

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Beyond personal grief and injury, which five financial expenses ripple out from traffic collisions?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: One serious wreck drains lost paychecks, hospital and rehab bills, support services, and repair costs.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Against what travel measure are collision and fatality totals compared to judge safety fairly?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Measuring crashes per miles driven shows real risk better than raw counts on busy versus quiet roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: Which four driver choices appear on the guide's list of leading Louisiana traffic-fatality causes?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Every one of those four fatal factors—drinking, phones, road rage, and skipping belts—is completely preventable.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Why must drivers stay mindful of how pedestrians and bicyclists experience the same street?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: A wide multi-lane arterial that feels effortless inside an SUV feels exposed on foot or two wheels.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What should an alert driver always expect from other people using the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Assuming everyone will yield or stay in their lane leaves you flat-footed when someone blunders.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: In which four performance areas do different vehicle types handle differently?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: A loaded delivery truck cannot corner, brake, or accelerate anywhere near a compact hatchback.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which four factors on an individual car change how safely it handles on the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Even two identical sedans stop very differently when one runs bald tires and worn shocks.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Why should a car-only driver still learn how heavy trucks and motorcycles handle?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Knowing truck stopping limits and motorcycle swerve hazards stops you from crowding them in traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: On which types of highways do unsafe speeds create especially severe hazards?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: High kinetic energy and fast traffic flow magnify speed mismatches on freeways and expressways.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: Which three conditions can make driving below the posted speed limit still dangerously fast?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Posted signs assume clear dry conditions and an alert driver, not downpours, gridlock, or exhaustion.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: What two traffic forecasts guide engineers when choosing lane counts, shoulders, and medians?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Heavy freight corridors get wider lanes, stronger pavement, and broader shoulders than quiet local streets.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Which local government authority maintains and regulates a Louisiana parish road?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Louisiana uses parishes where other states use counties, so parish government handles local parish roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Which government authority regulates a Louisiana state highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: State highway agencies set signage, maintenance, and speed rules along state-numbered routes.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: How do United States numbered highways relate historically to the Interstate Highway System?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Older U.S. routes often pass right through town centers and stoplights because they were built before Interstates.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: What traffic scale and geographic reach define the Interstate highway system?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Controlled-access Interstates move high-volume long-distance passenger and freight traffic from coast to coast.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Which compass directions correspond to even-numbered versus odd-numbered Interstate highways?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Across Louisiana, even-numbered Interstate ten runs east-west while odd-numbered Interstate fifty-five runs north-south.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How is an expressway divided, and at least how many lanes does it carry?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Expressways separate opposing high-volume flows and provide at least two lanes each way.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: What alternate word does the Louisiana guide use interchangeably with expressway?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Knowing the manual treats freeway and expressway as synonyms avoids overthinking exam wording.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What defines a toll road, and what two payment methods does the guide mention?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Drivers fund toll bridges and turnpikes per trip using either toll tickets or electronic prepaid passes.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: What visual and median features distinguish a parkway in the Louisiana guide?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Parkways pair a divided roadway layout with substantial surrounding trees and scenic landscaping.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: What physical feature separates opposing traffic directions on a divided highway?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Grass medians, cable barriers, or concrete walls block head-on crossovers between opposing lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Where are vehicles allowed to enter and exit a limited-access highway?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Channeling merges onto signed entrance and exit ramps eliminates surprise cross-street T-bone conflicts.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Which connections does a partial-access road allow, and which direct openings does it exclude?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Eliminating private residential and business driveways cuts constant curb pull-outs while keeping cross streets.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: How does exit-only ramp access differ from roads built with street or driveway connections?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Full ramp control keeps high-speed through lanes insulated from slow local driveway turns.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: How do wider shoulders alongside gentler curves and hills affect crash rates?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Gradual bends and paved recovery room let a drifting tire return smoothly instead of rolling.
sec03-card-sec03-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Wider shoulders, gentler curves cut crashes

visual_sync.text_span: Wider shoulders, gentler curves cut crashes

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: Why do highway designers clear fixed obstacles away from the roadside?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Sliding onto open grass hurts far less than striking an unguarded pole or culvert beside the fog line.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: What two traction and braking benefits come from well-maintained, sound pavement?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Even, intact asphalt keeps tire rubber planted firmly on the surface during hard braking.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: Which three surface or edge defects appear on poorly maintained roads?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Hitting deep ruts, potholes, or a steep pavement edge can blow a tire or yank steering.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Does it take a heavy downpour to cut tire traction, or can a light drizzle do it too?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Early drizzle lifts road oil and dust into a slick film before heavy rain washes it off.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: What happens between your tires and the pavement during hydroplaning?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Once water wedges beneath the tread faster than grooves channel it out, steering and braking vanish.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: What is the purpose of roadway drainage engineering?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Sloped crowns and roadside drains shed standing puddles before highway tires hydroplane.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.question_text: How do pavement grooves and rough surface textures help your tires?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.teaching_text: Micro-grooves give water an escape channel under tire treads so rubber stays biting pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-R18.question_text: Which three weather hazards can overhead electronic or dynamic message signs warn drivers about?
sec03-card-sec03-R18.teaching_text: Live digital boards alert you miles ahead before you drive blind into bridge ice or bayou fog.

sec03-card-sec03-R19.question_text: Why do highways in snowy regions build extra space alongside the travel lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-R19.teaching_text: Without snow-storage margins outside the shoulder, plowed banks would narrow live traffic lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-R20.question_text: Which three safety missions belong to the Federal Highway Administration?
sec03-card-sec03-R20.teaching_text: FHWA pairs engineering standards with public education campaigns aimed at lowering national highway fatalities.

sec03-card-sec03-R21.question_text: Which three types of controls direct driver actions and stopping at intersections?
sec03-card-sec03-R21.teaching_text: Combining hardware signals and signs with right-of-way rules keeps crossing streams from colliding.

sec03-card-sec03-R22.question_text: Through which three visual elements do traffic-control devices send their message?
sec03-card-sec03-R22.teaching_text: Recognizing a red octagon or yellow diamond at a glance lets you react before reading fine print.

sec03-card-sec03-R23.question_text: What coating feature on signs and lane stripes helps drivers navigate at night?
sec03-card-sec03-R23.teaching_text: Retroreflective beads bounce your own headlight beams right back so lane lines glow in darkness.

sec03-card-sec03-R24.question_text: Which four roadside or surface features work together to reduce collision severity?
sec03-card-sec03-R24.teaching_text: Poles that shear cleanly, energy-absorbing rails, grippy asphalt, and all-weather lines soften bad moments.

sec03-card-sec03-R25.question_text: What two lane-drift dangers do milled rumble strips warn a driver about?
sec03-card-sec03-R25.teaching_text: Sudden tire vibration and noise snap drowsy or distracted eyes back before wheels hit the ditch or oncoming cars.

sec03-card-sec03-R26.question_text: Which three engineering features are built to cut down intersection crashes?
sec03-card-sec03-R26.teaching_text: Separating turning cars, replacing T-bones with roundabouts, and coordinating green waves calm conflict points.

sec03-card-sec03-R27.question_text: To which four groups or assets does your legal and moral duty as a driver extend?
sec03-card-sec03-R27.teaching_text: Every turn of the wheel carries responsibility for people inside your cabin, everyone outside, and surrounding property.

sec03-card-sec03-R28.question_text: What two commitments sum up safe road sharing in the Louisiana manual?
sec03-card-sec03-R28.teaching_text: Pairing strict traffic-law obedience with the patience you want back diffuses road rage before it starts.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What three categories of roadside devices regulate traffic on Louisiana roads?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Every road relies on all three working together so drivers know lane rules, turns, and right-of-way without guessing.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: How quickly must you recognize traffic controls, and which category of signs must you obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Spotting posted controls late leaves zero time to brake smoothly or follow legal lane and speed commands.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: Which three groups of people giving live traffic directions on the road must you obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Human directors override normal routine flow whenever crashes, roadwork, or school crossings create immediate street hazards.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: Why does knowing a road sign's outer shape help you at long distance?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Glare, fog, or heavy rain can blur lettering while the silhouette still tells you what action awaits.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What two driving adjustments can you start making once you spot a sign's color and shape from afar?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Waiting until you are close enough to read small print forces last-second braking instead of smooth setup.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: Which sign exclusively uses an octagon shape, and what two actions does it demand?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Even snow-covered or viewed from behind at a cross street, eight sides always mean a mandatory full stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What four kinds of rules can rectangular regulatory signs govern along the street?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Tall white rectangles post enforceable local laws, from curb restrictions at the block edge to posted speed caps.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: What does a diamond-shaped road sign alert you to ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Seeing a tilted square on the horizon tells you to scan forward for changing road conditions immediately.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: What zone does an orange diamond warn you about, and how should you drive through it?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Crews and heavy equipment sit feet from active lanes, leaving zero margin for highway-speed mistakes.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: What examples of permanent road features or changes can yellow diamond signs warn about?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Permanent alignment shifts or hidden side-street entries catch drivers off guard unless they ease off the gas early.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Which sign owns the downward-pointing triangle, and what three steps must you take there?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Rolling briskly past a triangle without scanning cross traffic turns a merge into a right-of-way collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What roadway restriction does a sideways-pointing triangular pennant sign mark?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side of two-lane highways, the pennant stays visible even when trucks block right-shoulder posts.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: What sign category does a white railroad crossbuck belong to, and what exact legal duty does it carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Many learners mistake the X-shaped crossbuck for a mere warning when legally it carries full yield force.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What three message types can appear on a wide horizontal rectangular sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Wide boards fit long directional names, sharp turn chevrons, or lane-closure notices that tall panels cannot hold.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: How do route-marker shapes compare with standard stop, yield, warning, and regulatory shapes?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Distinctive shields let travelers spot interstate or state highway numbers instantly amid cluttered urban intersections.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: What core message does red communicate on stop, yield, do-not-enter, or wrong-way signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Across every sign family, red demands an immediate halt or warns that a movement is flatly illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: What kind of temporary roadway activity does an orange sign background warn drivers about?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Spotting orange ahead means normal lane habits pause because temporary work-zone setups can shift overnight.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: What mindset and response do amber backgrounds on warning or school signs require?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Amber flags areas where unexpected foot traffic or road geometry demands poised feet over the brake pedal.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: Which three specific regulatory sign types can use a black background?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: High-contrast dark panels make directional arrows, after-dark limits, and commercial restrictions pop under headlights.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: Which five light or bright sign background colors can carry black lettering?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Dark ink against bright reflective sheeting stays crisp in glaring noon sunlight and rainy twilight alike.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Which main class of traffic signs—plus certain highway number panels—uses a white background?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Clean white boards signal binding traffic rules like speed caps and turn bans rather than optional advice.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: On which five darker sign background colors can white lettering appear?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Bright white characters cut cleanly against deep backgrounds so highway exits and stop commands stand out at night.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: Along Louisiana highways, what four things can blue sign panels or route-marker sections identify?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: In coastal hurricane country, blue panels guide motorists not just to fuel or hospitals but vital storm evacuation corridors.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Which specific parking spaces are marked using light-blue signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Parking in an accessible stall without valid credentials blocks drivers who need ramp clearance and draws steep fines.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: How does a solid green sign background differ in meaning from green wording on a sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Overhead green panels point toward exits and cities, whereas green curb lettering spells out allowed parking windows.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: Which three vulnerable-user warning categories use fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Ultra-bright yellow-green glows during dim morning bell hours when kids and cyclists cross near distracted commuters.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: What kinds of destinations do brown guide-sign backgrounds point you toward?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Spotting brown ahead lets sightseers move smoothly toward exit lanes for state parks, historic sites, or campgrounds.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: What type of unexpected road situations do fluorescent pink sign backgrounds identify?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Unlike planned orange roadwork, bright pink warns of sudden emergencies like storm controls or crash closures ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: What three things ahead on the roadway do warning signs alert drivers to?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Advance alerts buy precious seconds to scan ahead before a blind hill, merge, or narrow bridge arrives.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: When you pass a warning sign, what two speed-control responses might the hazard ahead demand?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Treating a warning diamond as decoration leaves you carrying too much momentum if traffic is backed up around the bend.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: What shape, background color, and ink color do standard roadway warning signs usually use?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Consistent yellow diamonds with dark icons let drivers decode curves or merges in a split second.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: Which three crossing or zone warnings sometimes use fluorescent yellow to stand out?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Extra-vivid yellow draws your eyes to crosswalk edges where children or walkers step off the curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: Which sign category communicates enforceable traffic laws on direction, lane use, turns, speed, and parking?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Ignoring a regulatory panel is not skipping a tip—it is a ticketable violation that puts surrounding drivers at risk.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: What does a red circle with a diagonal red slash drawn across a black symbol mean?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Universal slash symbols instantly ban illegal U-turns, left turns, or truck entry without needing a single word.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: What two different legal speed rules can a speed-limit sign establish on a highway?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Crawling far below fast highway flow can trigger rear-end crashes just like speeding past the upper cap.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: When is driving at the posted maximum speed appropriate, and what three factors can require slowing down?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number during a Louisiana downpour or thick bayou fog can still be unsafe and unlawful.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: When does the lower speed on a School Speed Limit When Flashing sign apply, and what applies otherwise?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you slow during active beacons yet resume normal roadway pace once lights turn off.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: What do lane-use signs tell drivers, and in what two places can they be mounted?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Scanning overhead gantries and curb posts early keeps you from getting trapped in a mandatory turn lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: What markings painted directly on the road surface can reinforce lane-use signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Surface arrows confirm your lane's legal turn or straight path even when tall trucks block roadside posts.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.question_text: How many sides does a stop sign have, and what are its background and letter colors?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.teaching_text: No other traffic control shares that eight-sided red-and-white combination, eliminating hesitation at unfamiliar junctions.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.question_text: Where must your vehicle come to rest when a stop sign has a painted stop line or crosswalk?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.teaching_text: Rolling across painted bars blocks pedestrians on foot and noses your bumper into cross-street turn paths.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.question_text: Once you make a complete stop at a stop sign, what must you do before pulling out?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.teaching_text: Treating a quick brake tap as a free pass ignores cross-street cars and walkers who own the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.question_text: What does an All-Way or numbered-way plaque mounted beneath a stop sign tell you?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.teaching_text: Without that supplemental plaque, never assume cross-street traffic has a stop sign—they may hold full through priority.

sec04-card-sec04-F44.question_text: What colors and orientation identify a yield sign, and who gets to go first there?
sec04-card-sec04-F44.teaching_text: Forcing cross traffic to hit the brakes means you failed to yield right-of-way, even if you slowed slightly.

sec04-card-sec04-F45.question_text: What movement is a shared center left-turn lane built for, and what two uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F45.teaching_text: Using the middle lane as a passing chute risks a head-on wreck with oncoming drivers pulling in to turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F46.question_text: What is the maximum distance you may drive inside a shared center left-turn lane before turning?
sec04-card-sec04-F46.teaching_text: Cruising down the center lane past two hundred feet turns a short turn bay into a head-on collision alley.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: What must you do when a No Turn on Red sign is posted at your signalized corner?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Blind corners or heavy crosswalk traffic prompt engineers to ban red-light turns where sightlines hide oncoming hazards.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: What does a Stop Here on Red sign show an approaching driver?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Setback lines leave extra room so turning buses, trucks, or rail gates have space to swing clear safely.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: When no sign bans turning on red, what steps let you legally make a right turn on red?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Rolling a red right turn without halting behind the line first is one of the top automatic road-exam failures.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: What three vehicle actions does a Do Not Block Intersection sign forbid inside the box?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Stranding your car inside a cross street traps emergency rigs and gridlocks every green cycle around you.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: When backed-up traffic ahead prevents you from clearing an intersection completely, what must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Even a green light never lets you pull forward if bumper-to-bumper cars ahead will trap your tail in cross traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: What must you do before turning at a Left Turn Yield on Green sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: A circular green ball gives straight-through oncoming cars priority, so cutting across their path causes severe T-bone crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: How must traffic move on a street marked with One Way arrow signs?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Every lane on a one-way street flows together, so turning against the arrow puts you bumper-to-bumper with oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: What roadway rule does a rectangular Do Not Pass sign enforce?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Pulling out to overtake past that post gambles your life where hills, curves, or junctions hide oncoming cars.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: What visibility factor and hidden road features determine where engineers establish no-passing zones?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Crests, bends, side intersections, and driveways can launch an unseen vehicle into the oncoming lane mid-pass.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: What does a Pass with Care sign mark, and under what condition may you overtake there?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Leaving a restricted zone lifts the legal ban, yet you still own checking for clear sightlines and oncoming gaps.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: Where does a Keep Right sign direct your vehicle around medians, islands, or obstructions?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Veering left of a raised traffic island puts you straight into opposing head-on lanes on divided streets.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: On a multilane highway, which lane must you use at a Slower Traffic Keep Right sign if driving below normal flow?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Camping slowly in left lanes forces faster drivers to weave and pass on the right, multiplying blind-spot conflicts.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: What graphic appears on a Do Not Enter sign, and what does it forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Posted at freeway exit ramps and one-way mouths, that bold horizontal bar blocks you before you enter head-on lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: What urgent mistake does seeing a Wrong Way sign tell you about your vehicle's travel?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Spotting that red rectangle means oncoming headlights are heading straight toward your lane—pull off safely and turn around.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.question_text: Where are Wrong Way signs typically placed to catch drivers who missed an entry restriction?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.teaching_text: Engineers place them farther down ramps, one-way streets, alleys, and driveways as a second-chance warning.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.question_text: What purpose does a Louisiana highway-evacuation sign serve?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.teaching_text: Following marked evacuation corridors during hurricane orders keeps traffic flowing along policed, supported routes to safety.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.question_text: Where are railroad crossbuck signs required, and what right-of-way rule do they impose?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.teaching_text: Freight trains take up to a mile to halt, so drivers at every public crossing must yield without exception.

sec04-card-sec04-R18.question_text: What four types of travel info do guide signs share, and which three colors can they use?
sec04-card-sec04-R18.teaching_text: Color-coded panels sort navigation cleanly—green for routes, brown for parks, and blue for roadside services.

sec04-card-sec04-R19.question_text: What information do destination signs display for places like cities, airports, and borders?
sec04-card-sec04-R19.teaching_text: Knowing exact miles and lane arrows early stops last-second swerves across multiple highway lanes near interchanges.

sec04-card-sec04-R20.question_text: How can you tell from an overhead highway sign whether your upcoming exit ramp leaves on the left or right?
sec04-card-sec04-R20.teaching_text: Glancing at whether the small Exit panel sits top-left or top-right lets you merge lanes well before the gore.

sec04-card-sec04-R21.question_text: What accent color may appear on a left-exit sign, and why do highway designers add it?
sec04-card-sec04-R21.teaching_text: Because most freeway ramps peel off from the right lane, a yellow banner prevents drivers from missing a fast-lane exit.

sec04-card-sec04-R22.question_text: What colors appear on roadside service signs, and what amenities do they help travelers find?
sec04-card-sec04-R22.teaching_text: Spotting white hospital, fuel, food, lodging, or rest-area icons on blue panels keeps tired drivers from hunting exits.

sec04-card-sec04-R23.question_text: What do the shape and colors of a numbered route marker tell you about the road?
sec04-card-sec04-R23.teaching_text: Distinguishing an interstate shield from a parish or state highway marker confirms whether you are on the right class road.

sec04-card-sec04-R24.question_text: How should you use maps or navigation apps together with route markers in unfamiliar areas?
sec04-card-sec04-R24.teaching_text: Reviewing your route before rolling keeps your eyes scanning road shields ahead instead of staring down at a screen.

sec04-card-sec04-R25.question_text: What traffic changes do temporary incident signs warn about, and what sudden events cause them?
sec04-card-sec04-R25.teaching_text: Wrecks, chemical spills, or storm damage can block lanes without advance notice, demanding immediate speed drops.

sec04-card-sec04-R26.question_text: What exact background and lettering colors distinguish temporary incident-management signs?
sec04-card-sec04-R26.teaching_text: Permit questions love pitting fluorescent pink emergency boards against orange planned-construction diamonds.

sec04-card-sec04-R27.question_text: Which Louisiana safety law does the driver guide directly connect with roadside-incident warnings?
sec04-card-sec04-R27.teaching_text: Whenever incident signs appear ahead, expect police, tow trucks, or paramedics on the shoulder who need an empty buffer lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R28.question_text: What roadside hazards do orange work-area warnings signal, and what maneuvers may they require?
sec04-card-sec04-R28.teaching_text: Narrowed lanes and moving loaders leave zero buffer, so ease off early and prepare to stop or shift lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-R29.question_text: Beyond warning signs, what six other traffic-control tools or people guide cars through a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R29.teaching_text: Every cone, tube, drum, arrow board, and flag person forms a live lane boundary you must never cut across.

sec04-card-sec04-R30.question_text: Which color serves as the standard base color for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices?
sec04-card-sec04-R30.teaching_text: Whether on a diamond sign, plastic drum, or tall tube, bright orange always signals active roadwork zones.

sec04-card-sec04-R31.question_text: What shape are most work-area warning signs, and what second shape is also used?
sec04-card-sec04-R31.teaching_text: Diamonds warn of upcoming lane squeezes or crews, while rectangular orange panels often mark detours or zone ends.

sec04-card-sec04-R32.question_text: How must you respond as soon as you pass a Flagger Ahead warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R32.teaching_text: One-lane alternating work zones often halt traffic right around a bend where the flagger stands holding a paddle.

sec04-card-sec04-R33.question_text: What two adjustments should you make when you see a Workers Ahead sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R33.teaching_text: Shifting toward the far side of your lane and easing off the gas shields road crews working inches from traffic.
