sec04-card-sec04-R34.question_text: What hazard does a Low Shoulder sign warn about, and how should you handle slipping off the pavement?
sec04-card-sec04-R34.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel back onto a high asphalt lip can scrub a tire sideways and flip your car across oncoming lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-R35.question_text: What two baseline habits apply inside every highway work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R35.teaching_text: Dump trucks pulling into lanes or sudden flagger halts leave tailgaters no room to brake without piling up.

sec04-card-sec04-R36.question_text: Which two groups of people do reduced work-zone speed limits protect?
sec04-card-sec04-R36.teaching_text: Most work-zone crash injuries actually strike drivers and passengers inside cars, alongside vulnerable crews on foot.

sec04-card-sec04-R37.question_text: What happens to the dollar amount of traffic fines inside a Louisiana construction zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R37.teaching_text: Speeding or ignoring lane rules past orange cones hits your wallet twice as hard as an ordinary roadway ticket.

sec04-card-sec04-R38.question_text: Why must you stay alert even when driving through a familiar long-term construction project every day?
sec04-card-sec04-R38.teaching_text: Driving on autopilot based on yesterday's open lane can steer you straight into fresh overnight barrels or equipment.

sec04-card-sec04-R39.question_text: What two jobs do barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones, and tubes perform in a work area?
sec04-card-sec04-R39.teaching_text: Orange channelizing markers trace a temporary safe corridor around open trenches, drop-offs, and crew machinery.

sec04-card-sec04-R40.question_text: What extra visibility feature may be mounted on work-area drums, cones, or barricades at night?
sec04-card-sec04-R40.teaching_text: Mounted beacons help drivers read curved lane shifts in the dark long before low-beam headlights hit reflective tape.

sec04-card-sec04-R41.question_text: Which side should you pass on when diagonal barricade stripes slope downward to the left?
sec04-card-sec04-R41.teaching_text: Think of diagonal stripes like a rain gutter—follow the downward slant toward the open side of the road.

sec04-card-sec04-R42.question_text: Which side should you pass on when diagonal barricade stripes slope downward to the right?
sec04-card-sec04-R42.teaching_text: Reading stripe slant backward steers you toward the closed shoulder or trench instead of the open travel lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R43.question_text: What two messages do flashing or sequential arrow panels send during both daytime and nighttime roadwork?
sec04-card-sec04-R43.teaching_text: Bright LED chevrons cut through noon glare and midnight darkness alike, signaling early merges before a lane ends.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: What three vehicle movements do work-zone flaggers direct through roadwork?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Human flaggers coordinate one-lane alternating traffic around blind equipment where automated lights cannot adapt fast enough.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What hand tools do work-zone flaggers hold, and what color outer clothing do they wear?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: High-visibility orange vests paired with paddles or red cloth help drivers spot human crew chiefs early.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: From top to bottom, how are red, yellow, and green arranged on a vertical traffic signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Standard top-to-bottom lens order lets drivers with color-vision differences read every traffic light by position alone.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: From left to right, how are red, yellow, and green positioned on a horizontal traffic signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Sideways housings hung under low bridges always keep red leftmost so position cues stay predictable everywhere.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Under what condition does a steady green traffic light allow you to move forward?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Punching the gas on a fresh green without checking cross lanes invites crashes with late-clearing cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Who must a driver starting up on a new green light let finish crossing first?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Vehicles or walkers lawfully inside the box before the light changed still hold priority to exit safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Who must you yield to before turning left on a steady circular green light?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Unprotected left turns across fast oncoming lanes cause some of the deadliest urban intersection collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: When does a lighted green arrow allow you to drive in the direction it points?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Even a protected arrow requires verifying that straggling pedestrians or late cross-street cars have exited your path.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Even when turning on a green arrow, what opposing movement must you still watch out for?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Drivers facing red across the intersection may roll into the same cross-street lane you are turning toward.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: From which directions must turning drivers scan for pedestrians at an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Joggers and walkers can step into your target crosswalk from either curb corner or straight ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What does a steady yellow light warn, and what should you do if you can halt before the stop bar?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Flooring the accelerator to beat an aging yellow risks T-boning cross traffic launching on green.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What should you do if the signal turns yellow after your vehicle has already entered the intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes or reversing inside the box strands you right across cross-street lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What three actions does a flashing yellow traffic light require?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags high-conflict junctions where side-street entries demand lower speed and active scanning.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: At a flashing yellow signal, how must you handle vehicles that are already inside the intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Caution never means barreling past occupied lanes—let cars already mid-crossing finish before rolling forward.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What phase change does a steady yellow arrow warn of, and how must you respond?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Once protected arrow time expires, oncoming lanes or crosswalks are seconds away from receiving right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Where must you halt for a steady red light, and when may you move before green?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Stopping behind the painted bar or crosswalk keeps foot lanes open while you wait or check legal turns.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Under what three conditions may you turn right during a steady red signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Skipping the complete halt or overlooking a No Turn on Red plaque turns a routine corner into a citation.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Between what exact pair of street types does the Louisiana guide allow certain left turns on red?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Turning left on red onto or from a two-way street crosses active opposing lanes and is never legal.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Where a one-way left turn on red is allowed, who must you yield to before turning?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Pedestrians stepping off either curb beside or ahead of your hood hold priority over every red-phase turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Which roadside sign matches a flashing red traffic light, and what three steps must you follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Rolling through a blinking red without a complete stop violates right-of-way at rural and late-night crossings.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: When facing a lighted red arrow, when are you allowed to proceed in that arrow's direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red ball, a red arrow blocks movement in its direction until a green phase clears it.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: What kind of traffic flow do yellow center pavement markings separate?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Seeing yellow along your left side confirms that vehicles immediately across that stripe are heading straight toward you.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which side of a single broken yellow centerline must you drive on, and when may you cross it?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Dashed yellow allows passing or left turns only after verifying long, clear oncoming sightlines.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What maneuver do double solid yellow centerlines forbid, and what exception does the Louisiana guide allow?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that double yellow bars overtaking slow cars yet still allows turning into a driveway.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: On a two-lane road, what does a solid yellow no-passing stripe on your side of the centerline forbid?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Hills or bends ahead hide oncoming traffic from your vantage point even if the opposite lane has clear sightlines.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: In what two situations does the Louisiana guide allow crossing a yellow no-passing centerline?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Always read the stripe closest to your driver door to tell whether passing is legal from your lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: What traffic streams do white lane markings separate, and where should your car stay?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Straddling white stripes crowds neighboring lanes moving alongside you and triggers sideswipe crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What does a single solid white line between lanes warn about changing lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Solid white discourages weaving near intersections, tunnels, or merge tapers where sudden shifts surprise drivers.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: What does a wider-than-normal solid white lane line communicate compared to a standard one?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Extra-thick channelizing paint separates exit gore tapers or turn bays where late crossovers cause high-speed impacts.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: When may you move across a broken dashed white line between travel lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Even on routine dashed lanes, mirror checks, signals, and blind-spot glances come before easing across.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Which outer edge of the roadway does a solid white edge line mark?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Tracking the right-hand fog line keeps you on paved asphalt when oncoming high beams or rain wash out contrast.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: On a divided highway or ramp, which edge of the pavement can a solid yellow edge line mark?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Keeping yellow on your left and white on your right instantly confirms you are traveling the legal direction.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: What is the rule for double solid white lines separating lanes moving in the same direction?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Unlike a single solid white line, twin white stripes form a legal wall you may never weave across.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: What urgent danger do red raised pavement markers or reflectors shining back at your headlights mean?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Reflective studs shine white or yellow for legal traffic and flash bright red only to wrong-way drivers.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: What oversized white symbol and letters are painted on the lane ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Surface rail stencils alert you down at road eye line even when roadside signs sit behind foliage.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: At a marked railroad approach, what do the solid yellow centerline and white transverse bar each do?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Passing near tracks is outlawed, and halting behind the white crossline keeps your hood clear of lowering gates.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: Which lane should you normally travel in, and what three situations justify leaving it?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Staying right by default keeps left lanes open for passing, upcoming left turns, or overflow during right-lane backups.
sec05-card-sec05-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Right lane except pass, turn, traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Right lane except pass, turn, traffic

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: How must your speed in a left lane compare with traffic moving in the lane to your right?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Dragging behind right-lane pace turns the passing lane into a rolling roadblock that sparks risky weave passes.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Which lane does a vehicle traveling below the normal speed of traffic belong in?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Keeping slower vehicles tucked right lets main highway flow pass cleanly on the left with better visibility.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: What combination of yellow stripes outlines a shared center left-turn lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Solid outside edges combined with dashed inner lines mark a dedicated turn pocket shared by opposing directions.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Which directions of roadway traffic are allowed to pull into a shared center lane to turn left?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Because opposing cars share the exact same asphalt strip, scan far ahead before merging in to decelerate.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: What two through-traffic maneuvers are strictly forbidden inside a two-way center left-turn lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Using a two-way turn bay to jump traffic queues creates blind head-on conflicts with turning vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: What does a thick solid white line painted straight across your travel lane mark?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Pulling your front tires up behind the white bar protects crosswalk space and keeps cross-traffic corners clear.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: How are standard pedestrian crosswalks painted, and what extra stripes do high-visibility ones add?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Diagonal or ladder bars make busy school and downtown crossings pop from blocks away.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: What must drivers do whenever pedestrians are occupying a crosswalk?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Squeezing around walkers mid-crossing is illegal and risks hitting someone hidden by an adjacent stopped car.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: Do pedestrian crosswalks appear only at street corners, and what extra marker might accompany one?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Trails, campuses, and shopping districts often place signed crosswalks mid-block where drivers least expect to brake.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: What do white words or directional arrows painted inside a lane tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Surface ONLY legends and curved arrows commit your lane to a turn before you reach the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: What are your options when a single painted lane arrow points in more than one direction?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Combo straight-and-turn arrows give flexible routing, provided you signal turns early for drivers behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: If you realize you are already inside a mandatory turn lane when you wanted to go straight, what should you do?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Taking a sixty-second detour around the block beats cutting across live through-lanes at the last instant.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: Why is stopping inside a mandatory turn lane to wait for a gap back into through-traffic dangerous?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Drivers behind expect smooth turn flow and never anticipate a dead stop or abrupt sideways dart.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: What is a roundabout, and which stream of vehicles holds right-of-way at the entry?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Entering cars always yield to traffic already inside the circle so the ring never locks up.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: What speed does the Louisiana guide describe as adequate for driving through a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: Keeping speed at fifteen or below softens steering angles and gives everyone easy gaps to merge safely.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: From which direction do circulating vehicles approach that you must yield to before entering a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Counterclockwise flow sends every car inside the circle sweeping past your front bumper from the left.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.question_text: Why must you keep moving instead of stopping once you are circulating inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.teaching_text: Braking mid-circle to wave an entering car in triggers instant rear-end collisions from drivers curving behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.question_text: Which roadside signs help you identify and choose the right exit from a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.teaching_text: Checking advance destination boards before entering lets you count spokes calmly instead of weaving inside the circle.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.question_text: What three checks and signals should you perform right before leaving a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.teaching_text: Signaling right while scanning mirrors and outer lanes alerts waiting drivers and guards cyclists or crosswalk walkers.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: How does higher travel speed at the moment of impact affect injury risk?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Impact energy climbs steeply with every extra mile per hour, turning survivable bumps into severe trauma.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What happens to an unbelted rider's body right after the car slams to a stop in a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Even when crumpled steel halts the frame instantly, unrestrained riders keep moving at pre-crash highway speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What causes internal injuries inside the body even after a person hits the cabin interior in a wreck?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Stopping abruptly against a steering wheel or dash still leaves internal organs slamming forward inside the ribcage.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How do properly worn seat belts and restraints protect riders during a collision?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Spreading deceleration across strong bone structures lets riders slow down gradually with the vehicle's crumpling frame.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What two everyday habits does the Louisiana guide pair together to reduce crash trauma?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Short neighborhood errands cause plenty of wrecks, so clicking your belt and minding speed caps matter every drive.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which seating rows and vehicle types are covered by Louisiana's seat-belt requirement in the guide?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Skipping a belt in the back row of a pickup, van, or sedan still breaks Louisiana's occupant-restraint rule.
sec06-card-sec06-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Front and rear, cars, vans, pickups

visual_sync.text_span: Front and rear, cars, vans, pickups

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Where across your lower body should a lap belt sit, and what soft area must it stay off?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Riding high over your soft abdomen lets crash forces crush internal organs instead of anchoring strong pelvic bones.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How should the upper portion of a safety belt be routed across your upper body?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Tucking the diagonal strap behind your back or under your arm strips away upper-body crash protection.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Where does a fastened safety belt help keep riders during a rollover or hard collision?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Being thrown through a window onto pavement or under rolling metal multiplies fatality risk dramatically.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How does one unbelted backseat passenger endanger buckled riders up front during a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Crash momentum launches an unrestrained backseat rider forward into front seats with thousands of pounds of force.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Why does wearing a seat belt help the driver prevent a secondary crash right after a first impact?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Sliding across the seat on first impact leaves nobody able to steer or brake before hitting trees or traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What two criteria determine the right restraint for a child riding in a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Adult belts do not fit small frames, so kids need federally approved seats sized to their growth stage.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: When a child's age or size qualifies for more than one restraint category, which one does the guide say to pick?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Staying in the higher-protection seat stage longer shields developing necks and spines far better than rushing upgrades.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What two adult-and-child seating mistakes must you never make while traveling?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Human arms cannot hold a child against crash G-forces, and sharing one strap crushes the child between adult and webbing.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What unsafe posture on a vehicle seat is strictly off-limits for a child passenger?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Even routine firm braking for a dog or red light will hurl a standing child straight into the dashboard.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Do airbags replace the need to fasten your seat belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Without a belt holding you back, you slam forward into a rapidly inflating cushion or get thrown out in rollovers.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Which two clock-face hand positions on the steering wheel does the guide recommend with airbags?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Lower side grips keep your forearms clear of the center cover so a deploying airbag never flings hands into your face.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: At least how far back from an airbag-equipped steering wheel should the driver sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Airbags punch outward at explosive speed during the first few inches, so ten inches lets the cushion inflate safely first.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: If your steering column tilts, where on your body should you aim the wheel, and what should it point away from?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Directing the hub toward your breastbone lets the airbag catch your sturdy torso instead of striking your chin or face.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Why must you adjust your seat's head restraint before pulling out?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: A low-set headrest acts like a pivot in a rear-end hit, letting your neck snap backward violently.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How does active vehicle safety tech differ from passive occupant protection?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Braking and stability aids work before contact to dodge wrecks, whereas belts and crumple zones shield you during impact.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What do reverse sensors and backup cameras help a driver detect?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Low bumper blind zones can hide toddlers, pets, or bollards invisible through high rear glass—though head checks still rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What kind of traffic danger does blind-spot warning equipment assist with?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Radar chimes catch cars tucked beside your rear quarter panel, supplementing—never replacing—your over-the-shoulder glance.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What mistake does a lane-departure warning system alert you to?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Camera sensors catch tired or distracted drifting across painted stripes when no turn signal was switched on.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What adjustment does adaptive cruise control handle automatically behind traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Forward sensors ease throttle or brake to hold your chosen time cushion when highway traffic slows ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: What two outcomes can automatic emergency braking help achieve when a hazard appears ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Shaving even a fraction of a second off reaction lag can avoid bumper contact or dramatically lower impact speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: When does traction-control equipment step in to assist the driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Modulating power or braking a slipping wheel helps your tires bite wet or loose pavement during acceleration.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: At what critical moment does electronic stability control intervene?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: By braking individual wheels when sensors detect sideways yaw, stability control helps keep your car pointed where you steer.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What does the vehicle-safety term crashworthiness measure?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Strong cabin cages paired with energy-absorbing ends determine how well riders survive violent collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: How do front and rear crumple zones protect people riding inside the cabin?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Letting outer metal fold like an accordion soaks up kinetic shock before it reaches the rigid passenger cell.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: What safety role does interior cabin padding serve during a collision?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Softened dash, pillar, and door panels cushion secondary impacts if arms, knees, or heads swing forward.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What hazard inside an SUV, van, or wagon can a cargo barrier help block?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Unstrapped toolboxes or luggage become flying projectiles under hard braking unless a partition holds them aft.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: What four pieces of vital info do your vehicle's lights and reflectors broadcast to surrounding drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Working lamps and reflectors let others read where you are, how wide your rig is, and when you brake or turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: How soon should you repair a mechanical defect that could compromise safe driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Putting off spongy brakes, bald tires, or dead signals turns a minor repair bill into a highway emergency.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: Why should you inspect your vehicle before heading out on a trip?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Catching a soft tire or fluid puddle in your own driveway beats breaking down on an interstate bridge.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: At least how deep must tire tread measure on the Louisiana guide's weekly vehicle checklist?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Grooves shallower than one sixteenth of an inch cannot channel rainwater away, inviting skids and blowouts.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: Beyond tread depth, what four kinds of tire damage or wear should you check for?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Sidewall blisters or peeling rubber warn of structural casing failure that can burst at highway temperatures.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: How do you verify your engine has the right amount of motor oil?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Running below the dipstick crosshatch starves moving engine parts of lubrication and risks seizing the motor.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: What battery flaws and engine-bay warning signs should you look for during a hood check?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Crusty battery posts cause sudden no-starts, while dripping hoses can overheat the motor or spark under-hood fires.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: What two things must you verify on your headlamps, rear lamps, and turn signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Burned-out bulbs hide your moves, and cracked lenses let water short sockets or glare white light illegally.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: Along with lights and tires, what warning device, fuel part, and wearable items belong in routine checks?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: A working horn warns distracted drivers, a tight gas cap seals vapors, and sound belts keep alternators and straps safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: Which reflective and glass surfaces—especially what zone of the front glass—should you inspect for cracks?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Star cracks across the wiper path scatter oncoming headlights at night and shred rubber wiper edges.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: What two visual qualities must your vehicle's license plate maintain?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Mud, tinted covers, or peeled reflective coating that hides plate characters can draw a traffic stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: How must you handle used motor oil and old car batteries after maintenance?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Dumping waste oil or lead-acid batteries into trash cans or storm drains poisons Louisiana waterways and soil.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: Which two rear-warning light systems and what rain-clearing part should you test regularly?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Dead brake lamps invite rear-end hits, and dry-rotted wiper rubber smears water right when a storm breaks.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.question_text: Which three flat-tire and breakdown items in your vehicle should you inspect so they remain ready to use?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.teaching_text: Finding out your spare tire is flat on a dark shoulder turns a fifteen-minute swap into a long tow wait.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.question_text: Where should you look to find your car's under-hood fluid reservoirs and their target fill marks?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.teaching_text: Every engine bay places brake, coolant, and washer tanks differently, so the manual prevents pouring into the wrong cap.

sec06-card-sec06-F48.question_text: What temperature precaution and brake step should you take before inspecting under the hood?
sec06-card-sec06-F48.teaching_text: Pressurized hot radiators can scald skin instantly, and setting the parking brake stops the car from rolling.

sec06-card-sec06-F49.question_text: Before climbing into the driver seat, where should a quick walk-around inspection check?
sec06-card-sec06-F49.teaching_text: Ten seconds walking around catches toys, curbs, fluid drips, or small children hidden below bumper sightlines.

sec06-card-sec06-F50.question_text: Before turning the key or pressing start, what five cabin setup steps belong on your routine?
sec06-card-sec06-F50.teaching_text: Setting seats, mirrors, locks, clean glass, and belts while parked keeps both hands focused once rolling.

sec06-card-sec06-F51.question_text: What reach test tells you your driver seat is positioned at the right distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F51.teaching_text: Sitting too far back makes your foot stretch short of full emergency brake pressure when seconds count.

sec06-card-sec06-F52.question_text: Right before pulling away, which dashboard readouts and visibility items should you confirm?
sec06-card-sec06-F52.teaching_text: Spotting a warning light or empty washer tank before leaving saves getting blinded by road spray mid-trip.

sec06-card-sec06-F53.question_text: What personal readiness standard applies before every drive, and when must you refuse the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F53.teaching_text: Exhaustion, emotional distress, alcohol, or drowsy medication dulls judgment long before you notice your own lag.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: When is the only safe time to slide or tilt the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Unlatching a seat track in motion can slide you suddenly off the brake pedal and yank the steering wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How should the head restraint line up when you lean back against the seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Catching the back of your skull squarely stops violent backward neck hyperextension in a rear-end crash.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How should your elbows and knees look when holding the steering wheel and pressing pedals?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Locked-straight joints transmit crash shock straight into bones and limit quick steering leverage.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Where does the guide recommend resting your right heel as you switch between gas and brake?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Pivoting smoothly on a planted heel gives precise pedal modulation instead of stomping clumsily from midair.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How should you press the accelerator when pulling away and building cruising speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Flooring the throttle wastes fuel, spins tires on damp asphalt, and surges unpredictably in traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: What instrument glance should you repeat periodically while cruising along the road?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Smooth modern highways mask velocity, letting cars creep ten over the limit unless you verify your gauge.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What two-step pedal action gives smooth, controlled deceleration?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Lifting off early and squeezing the brake progressively flashes early brake lights so trailing cars never panic-stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What visual landmark tells you that you left enough gap when stopped behind another car in traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Keeping their rear tire bottoms in sight stops a rear-end hit from shoving you into them and lets you steer around stalls.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: What sequence of checks and signals must you complete before pulling out into live traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Flipping a blinker on never grants right-of-way—you must wait for both sidewalk walkers and street gaps first.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Instead of trusting mirrors alone, how must you look when backing your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Interior mirrors frame a narrow tunnel, whereas turning your head opens wide peripheral views behind both rear corners.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Why must you never twist the ignition to the lock position while a vehicle is still moving?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Snapping the steering lock mid-roll freezes your front wheels instantly so you cannot steer around curves or hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: In the guide's three-part skill model, what does physical driving skill focus on?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Smooth hand-eye-foot muscle memory lets you steer, signal, and brake cleanly without looking down at pedals.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What aspect of driving does social driving skill cover?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Sharing merges calmly, signaling early, and yielding without ego keeps minor traffic mistakes from escalating into wrecks.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: What two ongoing habits define mental driving skill behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Anticipating another driver's sudden lane dart before it happens separates proactive safe drivers from reactive ones.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: Which three maintenance items does the guide highlight for fuel-efficient driving?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Underinflated tires add rolling drag while dirty engines or wrong-viscosity oil burn extra gas every mile.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: What three everyday loading, errand, and parking habits save fuel?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Hauling dead trunk weight, running cold-start single errands, and sitting parked with the motor running burn gas for zero miles.
sec06-card-sec06-R16.must_match_memory_hook: Lighten trunk, group trips, cut idling

visual_sync.text_span: Lighten trunk, group trips, cut idling

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: How can planning when and where you drive reduce fuel consumption?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Stop-and-go rush-hour gridlock guzzles far more fuel than cruising steadily outside peak traffic windows.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: In what two places on or in your vehicle do you find its recommended tire inflation pressure?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Tire sidewalls print maximum burst ratings—not your vehicle's target pressure printed on the driver door placard.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: What happens to the car's turn angle and tire grip during oversteer?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: When back tires lose bite first, the tail swings wide and points the nose tighter into the corner than steered.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: What happens to the car's turn angle and tire grip during understeer?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Entering a wet curve too fast overwhelms front-tire grip so the nose pushes wide toward the outside edge.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: Why does the guide warn against slamming the brakes during an oversteer skid?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Sudden braking shifts vehicle weight forward onto the nose, unweighting the rear tires and spinning the tail faster.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: How do your hands and arms move during the hand-to-hand steering method?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Sliding and feeding the rim side-by-side keeps your forearms clear of the airbag cover throughout highway bends.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: For which two driving maneuvers does the guide describe using hand-over-hand steering?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Sharp intersection corners and parking-lot stalls need rapid large wheel rotations while speeds stay very low.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: In what two brief situations is steering with one hand acceptable according to the guide?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Outside twisting to back up or tapping wipers or lights, two hands belong on the rim at all times.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: What three geometric parts make up every roadway corner?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Breaking a bend into entry, clipping point, and exit helps you finish slowing before you bend the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: Where should your eyes look and when should you set your speed for an upcoming bend?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Scanning far around the curve reveals tightening radii or stalled cars while you still have straight pavement to brake.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: What kind of entry speed and control style keep a car planted around a curve?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel or jabbing brakes mid-bend spikes tire load past available grip and triggers a skid.

sec06-card-sec06-R28.question_text: If you double your speed going into a curve, how much does the sideways cornering force multiply?
sec06-card-sec06-R28.teaching_text: Physics squares centrifugal pull—going twice as fast demands four times the tire grip to stay on the road.

sec06-card-sec06-R29.question_text: How should you operate steering, brakes, and gas while rounding a curve?
sec06-card-sec06-R29.teaching_text: Gentle, blended inputs let suspension weight settle evenly across all four contact patches.

sec06-card-sec06-R30.question_text: What two immediate adjustments must you make as soon as rain wets the pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-R30.teaching_text: Wet asphalt stretches stopping distance dramatically, so normal dry-weather following gaps leave zero margin.

sec06-card-sec06-R31.question_text: Why can the first light drizzle make a dry road surprisingly slick?
sec06-card-sec06-R31.teaching_text: Light rain floats weeks of dripped engine oil and rubber grime into a greasy film before heavy downpours wash it off.

sec06-card-sec06-R32.question_text: Which three groups of unprotected road users appear in much higher numbers when warm weather arrives?
sec06-card-sec06-R32.teaching_text: After cooler months, drivers must retrain mirror and intersection scans for narrow bicycle and motorcycle profiles.

sec06-card-sec06-R33.question_text: Why must drivers read warning labels carefully before taking seasonal allergy medicines?
sec06-card-sec06-R33.teaching_text: Over-the-counter antihistamines can trigger heavy drowsiness, blurred focus, or dangerous drug interactions behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R34.question_text: What damage can potholes cause, and what two dangers hide in large roadway puddles?
sec06-card-sec06-R34.teaching_text: Deep standing water can mask rim-bending craters, soak brake rotors, or lift your tires clean off the asphalt.

sec06-card-sec06-R35.question_text: Who must you never leave waiting inside a parked vehicle during warm or hot weather?
sec06-card-sec06-R35.teaching_text: Louisiana sun turns a closed cabin into a lethal oven within minutes, even with windows cracked slightly.

sec06-card-sec06-R36.question_text: What under-hood and vehicle check should you complete before setting out on a hot-weather drive?
sec06-card-sec06-R36.teaching_text: High summer heat stresses cooling systems and engine oil hard, turning low coolant into a highway boil-over.

sec06-card-sec06-R37.question_text: What does a vehicle's rated payload capacity measure?
sec06-card-sec06-R37.teaching_text: Overloading past payload limits strains tires, lengthens braking distances, and destabilizes emergency handling.

sec06-card-sec06-R38.question_text: What three work-zone elements should you watch for when seasonal highway projects ramp up?
sec06-card-sec06-R38.teaching_text: Fresh resurfacing crews and slow dump trucks appear abruptly on routes that stayed wide open all winter.

sec06-card-sec06-R39.question_text: Which two neighborhood features demand renewed attention as soon as the school year starts?
sec06-card-sec06-R39.teaching_text: Routes quiet all summer suddenly fill with buses, flashing beacons, and young walkers at morning and afternoon bells.

sec06-card-sec06-R40.question_text: How do wet fallen leaves change the grip of a roadway?
sec06-card-sec06-R40.teaching_text: Soggy leaf mats act almost like patches of ice, hiding lane paint and stretching stopping distances.

sec06-card-sec06-R41.question_text: Why must you never park your car on top of dry leaf piles?
sec06-card-sec06-R41.teaching_text: Exhaust converters underneath your floorboard glow blistering hot and easily ignite dry leaves packed underneath.

sec06-card-sec06-R42.question_text: How does earlier sunset affect spotting walkers and cyclists—even on streets you know by heart?
sec06-card-sec06-R42.teaching_text: Familiarity breeds complacency right when dusk shadows cloak dark clothing along neighborhood shoulders.

sec06-card-sec06-R43.question_text: Why do seasonal temperature swings require rechecking your tires, and what two things should you inspect?
sec06-card-sec06-R43.teaching_text: Cooling air contracts inside rubber casings, dropping PSI and hurting wet-weather grip if left unchecked.

sec06-card-sec06-R44.question_text: How should you adjust speed and controls when driving through heavy standing water?
sec06-card-sec06-R44.teaching_text: Hard braking or sharp wheel tugs in deep water break the last shred of tire contact with pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-R45.question_text: What exact steering and pedal response recovers grip if your car starts hydroplaning on water?
sec06-card-sec06-R45.teaching_text: Gently lifting off the throttle lets speed bleed down until tread grooves sink back through the water wedge.

sec06-card-sec06-R46.question_text: During rain, snow, or fog, what key safety advantage does switching your headlights on provide?
sec06-card-sec06-R46.teaching_text: Low beams light both headlamps and rear taillights so approaching and trailing cars spot your silhouette through spray.

sec06-card-sec06-R47.question_text: What is the safest trip choice in severe winter weather, and what five systems must work if you have to go?
sec06-card-sec06-R47.teaching_text: If canceling is impossible, verify brakes, wipers, defroster, lights, and cabin heater before leaving.

sec06-card-sec06-R48.question_text: Why must you lower speed and stretch out your following gap on icy or snowy roads?
sec06-card-sec06-R48.teaching_text: Packed snow and glaze ice multiply braking distance several times over, turning normal gaps into guaranteed pileups.

sec06-card-sec06-R49.question_text: Which exterior parts of your car must be cleared of snow and ice before driving off?
sec06-card-sec06-R49.teaching_text: Peephole scraping leaves blind zones, and roof slabs blow backward into trailing windshields or slide down under braking.

sec06-card-sec06-R50.question_text: Do winter snow tires make driving at normal dry-weather speeds safe on ice or snow?
sec06-card-sec06-R50.teaching_text: Cold-weather rubber helps traction marginally, yet ice still offers a fraction of dry pavement's stopping grip.
sec06-card-sec06-R50.must_match_memory_hook: Winter tires never justify normal speed

visual_sync.text_span: Winter tires never justify normal speed

sec06-card-sec06-R51.question_text: Which three roadway locations freeze before regular pavement and stay icy longer?
sec06-card-sec06-R51.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and below Louisiana bayou bridges and elevated spans while nearby ground-warmed asphalt stays wet.

sec06-card-sec06-R52.question_text: In heavy rain, how can your windshield wipers tell you whether you are driving too fast?
sec06-card-sec06-R52.teaching_text: If sheets of water blur forward sightlines faster than high-speed blades can sweep, ease off immediately.
sec06-card-sec06-R52.must_match_memory_hook: Slow until wipers keep glass clear

visual_sync.text_span: Slow until wipers keep glass clear

sec06-card-sec06-R53.question_text: What six emergency items does the guide recommend packing for cold-weather travel?
sec06-card-sec06-R53.teaching_text: Basic warmth, hydration, light, ice tools, and first-aid gear keep passengers safe during long winter highway closures.
sec06-card-sec06-R53.must_match_memory_hook: Blankets, water, food, light, scraper, aid

visual_sync.text_span: Blankets, water, food, light, scraper, aid

sec06-card-sec06-R54.question_text: What does the guide instruct you to do if winter weather strands your car along the road?
sec06-card-sec06-R54.teaching_text: Your cabin shelters you from freezing wind and gives rescue crews a large target far easier to spot than a walker.

sec06-card-sec06-R55.question_text: Does clear mild weather ever let a driver stop monitoring surrounding road conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-R55.teaching_text: Sudden gulf storms, road debris, or unpredictable drivers can turn a sunny afternoon hazardous in seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which five internal, social, cabin, and roadway factors shape how a person drives?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Loud friends in the back seat and peer pressure sway split-second choices just as strongly as wet asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: How does a defensive driver time hazard responses compared with a passive driver?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Spotting trouble forming three blocks ahead beats slamming brakes after an emergency already traps you.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Which two sets of boundaries—human and mechanical—does a defensive driver always respect?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Overestimating either your own night reflexes or an older sedan's wet-braking grip invites avoidable wrecks.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How does defensive driving combine personal accountability with awareness of surrounding traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Driving lawfully yourself solves half the puzzle—leaving margin for someone else's mistake solves the rest.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Before turning the key, how should you prepare riders, pets, and vehicle doors?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Loose dogs jumping onto laps cause swerves while locked doors stay latched during rollover impacts.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Why isn't speeding the sole pace mistake that raises crash risk?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Crawling far below highway flow creates sudden closing-speed traps and panicked lane-dives behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Before heading out to an event where alcohol is planned, what ride arrangement comes first?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Picking a zero-alcohol driver before the first drink avoids impaired rationalization at midnight.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What four lane, turning, or traffic-light clues suggest another motorist may be impaired?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Recognizing erratic lane drift or bizarre delays at green lights early gives you time to stay clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: How does Louisiana's guide recommend putting safe distance between yourself and a suspected impaired driver?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Peeling onto a side street or highway exit beats trying to outrun an unpredictable swerver ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: What two competitive impulses must you avoid when merging or sharing right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Yielding three car-lengths costs two seconds while fighting over a merge taper crushes fenders.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: When should you alert law enforcement after spotting reckless or suspicious driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: A prompt call from a safe stop lets troopers intercept a wrong-way or impaired driver before tragedy.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: In Louisiana's five-step defensive routine, what three continuous eye actions define the opening step?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Active moving eyes spot developing trouble well ahead of the hood before step two even begins.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What are you actively pinpointing during the identify phase of the five-step defensive routine?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Flagging blind curves, gravel patches, and creeping driveway noses separates harmless scenery from real threats.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What question does your brain ask during the prediction phase of the five-step routine?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Asking whether that rolling sedan will run its stop post prepares your foot before metal meets.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: How do the final two steps of the five-step defensive routine work together to prevent a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Picking whether to brake, steer, or tap the horn comes first—smooth physical inputs finish the save.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Which four personal qualities does Louisiana's guide highlight as hallmarks of a defensive driver?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Sharp eyes and early anticipation pair with calm judgment and practiced car control on every drive.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What two commitments—attention and abstinence—keep a driver genuinely alert?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Even mild sedatives or alcohol dull the fine-detail scanning that keeps defensive drivers safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How does your following distance reflect whether you are truly anticipating hazards?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: An open cushion ahead proves you expect sudden stops rather than gambling on instant reflexes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: From which four sources should you weigh potential trouble before an emergency maneuver is forced?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Checking bald tires or storm clouds early prevents mechanical and weather surprises from stacking up.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: How does sound driving judgment treat posted speed limits when bad weather rolls in?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Posted signs assume dry clear pavement—real judgment drops speed well underneath during storms.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Which two oncoming or overhead controls must you never try to outrun?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Flooring the gas to beat crossing bells or a stale yellow gambles lives to save sixty seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: What separates a smart passing choice from a reckless gamble?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Staying behind a slow tractor thirty extra seconds beats forcing a tight two-lane pass.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: How do heavy stress and strong emotions distort behind-the-wheel choices?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Anger, grief, or anxiety hijacks calm risk calculation and pushes drivers into rash lane cuts.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Why do steady lane positioning and predictable driving help everyone around you?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Smooth signals and centered tracking let surrounding motorists read your next move effortlessly.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What should you do when intense emotional distress leaves little bandwidth for traffic demands?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Sitting parked ten minutes to breathe and settle beats carrying emotional overload onto busy streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Which two mental faculties drop—and what happens to reflexes—when fatigue sets in?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Drowsy brains miss brake lights and road signs seconds longer than rested drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: What terrifying event can extreme exhaustion trigger while your hands still hold the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Four seconds of microsleep at sixty-five miles per hour sends an unsteered car across an entire football field.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What two smart steps come before departing on any long highway drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Combining poor sleep with an allergy pill guarantees highway drowsiness within the first hour.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: How should you structure breaks and clock hours when planning a road trip?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Driving across your body's normal overnight sleep window fights circadian biology mile after mile.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What is the sole safe move when you can no longer keep yourself awake on the highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Cold air and loud music mask fatigue only minutes—pulling off into a safe well-lit rest stop saves lives.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How should you set arrival expectations when mapping out a long drive?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Unrealistic arrival promises pressure tired drivers into skipping breaks and pushing past safe speeds.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How often does Louisiana's guide recommend stopping to step out and stretch on long drives?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Memorize two hours—walking briskly every one hundred twenty minutes restores circulation and eye focus.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: When two licensed drivers share a road trip, how often—and when—should they swap seats?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Rotating at two-hour marks before tiredness hits keeps every shift behind the wheel fresh.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Between which exact overnight hours does Louisiana's guide urge limiting travel?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Human alertness hits its deepest biological trough between midnight and six in the morning.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: What three physical face or head sensations warn that dangerous drowsiness has arrived?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Fighting heavy eyelids means microsleep is seconds away—take the very next safe exit.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What three driving or mental lapses warn you are already too fatigued to keep rolling?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Realizing you cannot recall the last two exits or hitting rumble strips means pull off immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Must a medical condition be permanent to impair your driving, or do temporary illnesses and meds count too?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: A twenty-four-hour flu fever or single dose of cough medicine slows reaction time right away.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: How can nonprescription cold or allergy tablets interfere with safe driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Over-the-counter decongestants and antihistamines sedate reaction speed without needing a doctor's slip.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: When should you read a medication package's driving-related warning label?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Spotting a heavy-machinery drowsiness warning after you are already thirty miles down the interstate is too late.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Which two health professionals should you ask whenever a medicine's driving safety feels unclear?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Pharmacists and physicians catch hidden drug-to-drug drowsiness interactions across separate prescriptions before you ever drive.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Which four core driving abilities can prescription medications dull or distort?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Blurred sight, slowed foot speed, or dulled hazard judgment each raise crash risk sharply.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: Does developing a medical condition automatically end driving forever, or what step comes first?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Many conditions allow safe driving with simple daytime restrictions, corrective lenses, or treatment.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: How must applicants answer physical and mental health questions on Louisiana licensing forms?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Truthful disclosures match licenses with helpful safety restrictions rather than risking fraud revocations.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: What official state credential serves someone who surrenders driving privileges?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Swapping to a state identification card keeps full photo proof for banking and travel without driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: Which four everyday traffic violations define aggressive driving in Louisiana's guide?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Stacking speed with tight bumper-riding and unannounced lane cuts strips surrounding cars of escape room.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: What two aggressive moves around commercial trucks create especially severe crash danger?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Loaded tractor-trailers need hundreds of extra feet to slow and cannot see cars darting across No-Zones.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: What time-planning habit and two mood checks keep you from driving aggressively yourself?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Running ten minutes late turns every red light and slow merge into a self-made stress trigger.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: With what mindset should you view busy traffic instead of treating lanes like a contest?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Letting mergers in smoothly lowers cabin stress and gets everyone home intact.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: What three calm responses defuse another motorist who starts acting aggressively?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Staring back escalates a hothead into personal confrontation, whereas dropping back ends the interaction.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: Should you hold your ground against a tailgating bully or move safely out of their path?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Speeding up or blocking a lane turns an impatient stranger into a seventy-mile-per-hour hazard beside you.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: How should you react if an angry driver waves hostile gestures at you?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Returning a gesture takes hands off the wheel and pours fuel onto road rage.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: Which two retaliatory moves—with bumper or horn—must you never use to teach someone a lesson?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Your horn warns of crash danger—blasting or riding bumpers in anger provokes collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: Where should you drive if an aggressive motorist keeps following your car?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Uniformed officers or bright public storefronts with witnesses stop stalkers from approaching your window.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: Why must you never pull into your own driveway while an aggressive driver trails you?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: Pulling into an empty home driveway isolates you without help and reveals where you live.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: Should you ever pull onto the shoulder to step out and confront a persistent rager?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: Stepping out onto a highway shoulder turns a traffic dispute into a physical or weapon assault.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: How does Louisiana's guide draw the line between traffic violations and criminal road rage?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Aggressive driving breaks traffic statutes, whereas road rage crosses into criminal violence and assault.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.question_text: Which four deliberate intimidation or damage acts count as road-rage behavior?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.teaching_text: Pursuing, boxing cars in, intentionally scraping bumpers, or shouting threats all cross into road rage.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.question_text: What is the smart response right after another driver rudely cuts across your front bumper?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.teaching_text: Easing back two seconds restores your safety cushion instantly while retaliation doubles danger.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.question_text: Once clear of danger, what follow-up step helps protect other motorists from an aggressive driver?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.teaching_text: Sharing route, direction, and vehicle description from a safe spot helps officers intervene early.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What minimum same-direction lane count makes passing on the right permissible in Louisiana?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Two or more marked lanes flowing together provide dedicated asphalt without squeezing onto shoulders.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: May you dip onto a wide paved highway shoulder to pass a slower vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Even smooth asphalt shoulders stay off-limits for passing because stalled cars and debris wait there.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Why does overtaking on the right demand extra caution even when multi-lane rules allow it?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Passenger-side blind zones run wider, and slower left-lane drivers often drift back right unexpectedly.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: On a multi-lane highway, which lane is specifically meant for overtaking slower traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Using the far-left lane for passing keeps speed flow organized from right to left.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Why shouldn't you creep right up onto a slow truck's rear bumper before pulling out to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Crowding a wide trailer blinds you to oncoming cars until half your hood crosses the centerline.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Where should you wait while judging whether enough clear road exists ahead to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Hanging back preserves both forward visibility and room to accelerate smoothly before crossing left.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What oncoming sight should convince you to hold back rather than starting a two-lane pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Head-on closing speed cuts apparent highway distance in half—if you can see headlights ahead, wait.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Before pulling left to pass, why must you check mirrors and left blind spots behind you?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Swinging left without looking behind cuts directly into a faster car already in the passing lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Along with signaling left, what roadside pull-out points ahead must you scan before passing?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: A car nosing out of a rural driveway looks right before turning left—straight into your passing lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Where should your gaze stay—so your hands don't drift—while passing beside another car?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Staring sideways at the car you are passing pulls your hands subconsciously toward their door.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What visual check in your inside mirror proves you have cleared the passed car enough to pull back right?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Seeing their entire front grille in your center mirror guarantees safe bumper clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Do you only signal when pulling out to pass, or when returning right too?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Signaling your return alerts both the driver you passed and trailing cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How does Louisiana's guide advise helping another motorist complete a pass around you?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Lifting slightly off the gas shortens their exposure in the opposing lane and clears both cars faster.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Where inside your lane should you position your car when being overtaken on a two-lane road?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Giving wider lateral separation on narrow country asphalt protects mirrors if oncoming traffic appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Why aren't mirrors alone enough when shifting into reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Turning your body to look out the back glass covers wide blind zones that mirrors miss.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: At what pace—and with what braking readiness—should every reverse maneuver happen?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering makes fast backing twitchy—creeping at walking speed stops instantly if someone steps out.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What three hidden low hazards can a quick walk around your parked car uncover before backing?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Toddlers, sleeping pets, and bikes sit completely below trunk height out of mirror and window sight.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Why do the opening minutes of a rainstorm turn dry pavement unusually slippery?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Light rain lifts unwashed oil and grease droppings into a soapy sheen until heavy rain rinses it off.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Along with slower pace and extra caution, how much should you stretch following distance on wet pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Doubling your three-second dry gap gives wet tires room to stop smoothly without locking.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Where on a rainy roadway does slow, smooth driving matter most to prevent skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Sideways cornering load breaks wet tire traction far sooner than straight-ahead rolling ever does.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What three calm steps straighten out a vehicle that begins skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Gentle steering toward your intended lane center aligns front tires with where you want the car to roll.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: How should you treat the brake pedal during Louisiana's wet-road skid recovery?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Hitting brakes mid-skid locks sliding tires harder and kills the rolling grip needed to steer straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What happens between your tires and flooded asphalt when your vehicle hydroplanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Water pressure wedges underneath rubber faster than tread grooves can pump it clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which three core vehicle controls fail once hydroplaning lifts tires off asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Floating rubber cannot push sideways, pull forward, or scrub speed until tires settle back down.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: How do your feet, eyes, and hands regain pavement contact during hydroplaning?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Easing off the gas lets speed bleed naturally until tire weight sinks back through the water film.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Which one driving habit and two tire checks best prevent hydroplaning before it starts?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Crisp inflation and deep tread channels pump rainwater away as long as wet speed stays moderate.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What tire sound on rainy asphalt warns you to ease off your speed right away?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Hearing heavy water sloshing inside wheel wells means standing depth is building toward hydroplane speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Which ignition-key position must you never twist into while a vehicle is still rolling?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Clicking all the way to lock freezes the steering column solid so you cannot turn off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: How does your headlight beam reach set your maximum safe speed after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Outrunning your beam reach means any stalled car or deer appears closer than your brakes can halt.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: How does a dirty windshield hurt night vision when oncoming headlights shine?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Bug film and interior haze scatter oncoming beams across the whole glass like a glowing curtain.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: At least how much extra following time does Louisiana's guide add for routine night driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Adding at least one full second onto your daytime count offsets reduced depth perception in the dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: How many extra seconds of following distance should you add when driving an unfamiliar road at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Surprise curves and unmarked driveways on strange dark roads call for two extra seconds beyond daytime.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: From sunset to sunrise, may you cruise on parking lights alone or are full headlights required?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Dim parking bulbs only mark stationary cars—driving after sunset requires full low or high headlamps.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: Within what oncoming distance—and what following distance—must you dim high beams to low?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: High-beam glare inside those distances blinds oncoming drivers head-on and bounces straight off rear mirrors.
sec09-card-sec09-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: What windshield-clearing action automatically triggers Louisiana's daytime headlight law?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Any rain, mist, or road spray heavy enough for wipers requires turning full headlights on.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Even without wipers, below what weather visibility footage must your headlights turn on?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Thick fog, smoke, or dust cutting clear sight inside five hundred feet triggers mandatory headlights.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: How do you keep your lane safely when an oncoming driver refuses to dim bright headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Glancing down toward the white right-edge stripe saves night vision while keeping you centered.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: When must front fog lights turn off, and when are bright rear fog lamps reserved for?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Leaving bright rear fog bulbs blazing in clear night air mimics brake lights and dazzles followers.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does a flashing do-not-walk display split rules between walkers on the curb and walkers mid-street?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Turning drivers must still wait patiently while mid-crosswalk pedestrians finish reaching the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: What does a steady walk display authorize pedestrians at the corner to do?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Even with a steady walk icon, smart walkers still scan for turning cars before stepping out.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when your turning car meets a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk or on a walk light?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Sharing a green phase never lets right or left turners cut off people crossing on foot.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Whom must a driver turning right on red yield to before rolling across the corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Looking solely left for cross-traffic cars misses pedestrians stepping right in front of your hood.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: What is your duty even if someone steps across the street outside a legal crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: A pedestrian's jaywalking mistake never excuses striking a human being in the roadway.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Why is overtaking a vehicle halted at a crosswalk strictly forbidden?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Swinging into the next lane around a stopped truck or van strikes the pedestrian stepping out.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Approaching a stopped car near a corner, must paint be visible for a pedestrian crosswalk to exist?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Every street intersection carries legal unmarked crosswalk extensions even where no white stripes exist.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What two precautions apply near roadside walkers or children playing in yards?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Chasing a bouncing ball pulls kids into asphalt without a single glance toward traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: What head-check sequence should pedestrians use at the curb—and while walking across?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Looking left a second time checks the closest lane right before stepping off the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Does a blind pedestrian's white cane need a red tip to earn mandatory right-of-way—or what two aids qualify?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Whether plain white, red-tipped, or accompanied by a service dog, full priority always belongs to them.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: During which two low-speed vehicle moves must you take extra care near visually impaired pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Quiet modern engines give very little sound warning when backing out of driveways or arcing corners.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Which two pedestrian strips must your stopped bumper never block?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Stopping across a sidewalk apron forces blind walkers and wheelchairs out into live lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Why must you never honk your horn at a pedestrian with a visual impairment?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: A sudden horn gives zero directional clue of where safety lies and scrambles acoustic orientation.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: Which two road-user groups must you verify clear before turning right on a red light?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Scanning left for cars and right for walkers prevents the most common urban corner collision.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: How does a cell phone hijack all three—visual, manual, and cognitive—channels at once?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Texting combines all three distraction types simultaneously, making it deadlier than single-channel tasks.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: What two safe options handle an urgent phone call that cannot wait until your destination?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Handing the phone to a co-pilot or parking off the road keeps driving attention undivided.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: What two number-hunting or writing habits must never happen while rolling?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Looking down at a notepad or contact list blinds you to stopped cars ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: What should happen when an incoming phone call rings while you are driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Lunging for a ringing phone mid-turn causes panicked swerves over a call you can return later.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: Under what sole operating mode does Louisiana allow using a wireless device while driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Holding a phone in your hand while driving violates Louisiana's wireless-device restriction.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: Does Louisiana's ban on writing, sending, or reading texts apply strictly to teens or to every age?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Adults hold zero exemption—writing, sending, or even reading a text behind the wheel is illegal statewide.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.question_text: How does Louisiana law treat scrolling, reading, or posting to social-networking apps behind the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.teaching_text: Checking feeds or posting stories carries the exact same statewide ban across all ages as texting.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.question_text: Which specific Louisiana Revised Statute lists the narrow legal exceptions to wireless-device bans?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.teaching_text: Emergency-call reporting and parked-off-road exceptions live inside that specific section of state traffic law.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.question_text: Which four dangerous driving errors can negative peer pressure push a driver into?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.teaching_text: Showing off for loud friends spikes teen crash rates faster than almost any solo mistake.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.question_text: What three passenger-focused or horseplay behaviors does Louisiana's guide condemn?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.teaching_text: Swiveling your head to chat with backseat friends pulls your eyes and steering off the lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.question_text: How can supportive friends in the passenger seat actively boost trip safety?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.teaching_text: Good friends speak up calmly if you miss a speed drop or reach for a phone.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.question_text: As personal driving abilities shift with age or health, what two smart adjustments keep travel safe?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.teaching_text: Matching when and where you drive to current vision and reaction speed preserves safe independence.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.question_text: Who can review your full medication list to catch prescriptions that interfere with driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.teaching_text: Swapping timing or dosage with your clinician often keeps alertness sharp during daytime errands.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.question_text: What corrective-lens rule and two sensory checkups keep aging or changing drivers sharp?
