sec09-card-sec09-R29.teaching_text: Keeping glasses prescriptions current and hearing checked catches gradual changes before signs blur.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.question_text: Which time of day and weather window offer the safest margin when adapting trips?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.teaching_text: Daytime sunshine eliminates oncoming headlight glare and slick wet-pavement reflections that strain aging eyes.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.question_text: When pre-planning an easier route, what three lighting, turn, and parking features should you favor?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.teaching_text: Protected green-arrow left turns and pull-through parking stalls remove high-stress oncoming gap judgments.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.question_text: What two simple cabin-and-cushion habits buy extra reaction margin on every trip?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.teaching_text: Adding extra seconds ahead while muting radio clutter gives calm, unhurried braking room.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.question_text: How can experienced drivers refresh rusty habits and learn newer road designs like roundabouts?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.teaching_text: Traffic laws and vehicle tech evolve over decades, making periodic refresher classes valuable.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.question_text: When driving is no longer safe, what two mobility options keep someone connected?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.teaching_text: Sharing rides with family or catching transit preserves freedom without risking collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which two authorities must you obey whenever operating a vehicle on streets or highways?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Lawful traffic direction from an on-scene officer overrides standard routine flow during crashes or roadwork.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: How should you respond first when a law-enforcement officer signals you to stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Slamming brakes in a live lane panics everyone, whereas calm signaling to a safe shoulder protects all.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Which three documents must you be ready to hand over during a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Keeping registration and active insurance proof organized avoids fumbling through dark compartments beside live traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: During a traffic stop, where must you stay and how should you position your hands?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Stepping out uninvited or reaching under seats alarms approaching officers who cannot see inside tinted cabins.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: When does Louisiana's guide allow you to ask an officer stopping you to show identification?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Polite verification protects drivers when neither patrol markings nor a police uniform confirms official authority.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which three visual control systems govern traffic movement along every street?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Ignoring painted lane arrows while watching only overhead lights leads straight into wrong-lane conflicts.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How must every driver treat an intersection when its traffic lights go completely dark or out of order?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Assuming the wider street keeps right-of-way during power outages causes high-speed T-bone wrecks.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What standard of physical command must a driver keep over the vehicle at all times?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Loose steering habits, overloaded cabins, or aggressive stunts violate basic control duties even below speed limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What road conditions do posted speed limit signs represent, rather than guaranteeing safety anytime?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number through blinding rain violates safe-speed law despite matching the sign.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Which surface, sight, or traffic conditions require slowing below the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Water film, ice, fog, and packed bumpers shrink stopping margin far below dry-pavement design assumptions.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Why must you check your speedometer right after exiting a high-speed multilane highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: After miles at seventy, forty-five feels like crawling and tricks exiting drivers into speeding on ramps.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Which five real-world factors determine a reasonable speed under Louisiana's general speed rule?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Safe pace shifts mile by mile as neighborhood location, darkness, storms, and congestion change.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How must your speed stay bounded when a highway posts both maximum and minimum limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Creeping below a posted interstate minimum creates closing-speed hazards nearly as dangerous as speeding.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Even where no minimum speed sign stands, what slow-driving behavior is prohibited?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Rolling far below normal flow stacks impatient queues behind you and triggers risky passing maneuvers.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Around which three child-activity locations must you drop speed whenever children are outside?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Kids chasing balls or crossing with backpacks step off curbs impulsively without checking closing speeds.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How does Louisiana law treat racing, speed contests, and speed exhibitions on public roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Show-off launches and side-by-side pulls turn public lanes with cross streets into unguarded crash zones.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Where is the only lawful spot to cross over a divided highway's median or barrier?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Cutting across grassy medians drops mud onto fast lanes and surprises left-lane traffic head-on.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which four visual and signaling steps belong right before moving into another lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Scanning two lanes over catches cars merging into that same middle gap from the opposite side.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: What should you never do when you realize late that your turn or highway exit is right beside you?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Last-second swerves across solid gore lines cause rollovers when routing to the next exit costs minutes.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How should you handle a planned lane change when nearby traffic leaves no safe opening?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Nosing aggressively into tight bumper-to-bumper gaps triggers sudden chain-reaction braking and preventable sideswipes.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What should you do before changing lanes when a faster car is closing rapidly in that target lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Pulling ahead of a fast-closing vehicle forces hard braking even if bumper space looked open.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Where near an intersection does Louisiana's guide forbid changing lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Switching lanes approaching or crossing junctions blindsides turning cross-street drivers counting on your original lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: At least how many feet away must you stop from a school bus loading or unloading children?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Thirty clear feet keeps energetic kids visible well ahead of tall hoods and blind bumper corners.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: What do a school bus's flashing yellow lamps mean compared with its flashing red lamps and stop arm?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Accelerating on flashing yellow lamps gambles with kids stepping toward the curb seconds before red engages.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: Unless a specific roadway exception applies, which directions of traffic must stop for a school bus?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Children cross in front of the bus across opposing lanes just as often as stepping right.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: When does a bus pulled into a dedicated off-road loading zone not require passing roadway traffic to stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: When the bus sits completely off the street and walkers cannot cross lanes, conflict paths disappear.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Which three physical separators allow opposite-direction traffic to keep moving past a stopped school bus?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Only an impassable physical separator shields opposite lanes; painted double yellow stripes alone never qualify.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: On which multi-lane road setup with a dedicated two-way left-turn lane is opposing traffic exempt from stopping?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Louisiana exempts oncoming lanes when two travel lanes each way flank a dedicated center turn lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Must oncoming drivers stop for a school bus on a plain four-lane road lacking a barrier or turn-lane exception?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Test writers love this trap because four undivided lanes without a barrier or center turn lane still require stopping.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: On a three-lane road having one travel lane each way plus a center turn lane, who stops for a bus?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Never confuse three lanes with five because one lane each way plus a center turn pocket stops everyone.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Why should you ease off and cover the brake at intersections even when you hold right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Red-light runners and distracted cross-street drivers ignore legal rules, so defensive scanning saves your fenders.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Which four preparation steps come before you start turning at a corner?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Setting up lane position and blinkers early eliminates rushed blind-spot cuts right at the crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: At least how far before a turn must you both signal and be positioned inside the proper turn lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Louisiana pairs lane entry with signaling at one hundred feet so nobody dives late across lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Unless pavement markings allow dual right turns, which lane must you begin a right turn from?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Turning right from an inner lane cuts across curbside traffic continuing straight through the green.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Why must passenger-car drivers avoid swinging left right before turning right?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Swinging left tricks trailing drivers into thinking you are changing lanes left and invites right-side collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: When do you slow down for a turn, and where must your vehicle finish the turn?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Braking before the corner keeps tires planted so you exit cleanly without drifting across adjacent lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Why must your front wheels stay pointed straight ahead while paused waiting to turn left?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Pre-turning your tires left means any rear-end tap shoves your car head-on into oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: What danger comes from cutting a left-turn arc too sharply across the corner?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Slicing across the cross street's opposing lane puts your bumper nose-to-nose with cars waiting there.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Which maneuvers are legal once you enter a marked left-turn-only lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Going straight out of a turn-only pocket sideswipes through traffic expecting your lane to peel left.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How much clear visibility in both directions is required before turning around near a hill or curve?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Inside five hundred feet, cresting cars close the gap before a reversing vehicle can clear lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Who may use a shared center turn lane, and what maneuver is strictly banned inside it?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Using the shared center pocket to overtake slow traffic sets up head-on wrecks with opposing turners.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: At most how many feet may you travel inside a shared center left-turn lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Cruising blocks down the center lane turns a short turn pocket into a head-on collision chute.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Which four checks and signals belong right before merging into a shared center turn lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Checking ahead first spots oncoming drivers already pulling into that exact same shared pocket.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Before completing a left turn out of a shared center lane, which side-entry hazards must you watch?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out across stopped through lanes often nose straight into the center turn lane blind.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: In which direction does traffic circulate around the center island of a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Every entrance curves right so vehicles flow counterclockwise without head-on left turns across center.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: Between drivers entering a roundabout and drivers already circling inside, who yields?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Keeping the circular ring flowing prevents internal gridlock that would jam every connected street.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: When must you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Picking left, through, or right lane on approach sets your spiral exit path automatically inside.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Which two maneuvers does the guide forbid once you are inside a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Curved sightlines hide adjacent fenders, so lane swaps or passes inside circles cause instant sideswipes.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What guides you smoothly from your roundabout entry lane out to your intended street exit?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Multilane roundabouts paint spiral lane lines engineered to lead your chosen lane straight out safely.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: Besides circulating vehicles, whom else must you yield to at roundabout entries and exits?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Splitter-island crosswalks sit one car length back from the circle, requiring yield both entering and exiting.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: How must you position relative to a truck or bus navigating a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Long trailers straddle both circular lanes to clear tight center islands without climbing curbs.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: Which four planned vehicle actions require signaling to surrounding road users?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Warning others before shedding speed or shifting lanes prevents sudden rear-end and blind-spot surprises.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Which two methods may a driver use to communicate turn and stop signals?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Knowing left-arm signals keeps you legal and understood if a bulb burns out mid-trip.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: For at least how many continuous feet before a turn must your turn signal stay active?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: One quick flick right at the corner fails the hundred-foot rule and surprises trailing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: Which signal belongs on when pulling out from a right-hand parallel curb spot into traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: Signaling left alerts approaching lane traffic that your parked nose is about to merge outward.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.question_text: What signal is required before pulling out to the left to overtake a slower vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.teaching_text: A left blinker warns trailing drivers behind you not to start passing you at the same instant.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.question_text: Why must you never flash a one-sided turn signal to wave a trailing driver past you?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.teaching_text: Waving someone around with your blinker confuses oncoming traffic and shifts crash liability onto everybody.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.question_text: What maneuver are you signaling when you extend your left arm straight out horizontally?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.teaching_text: Pointing straight left mirrors the exact direction your front wheels are about to turn.

sec11-card-sec11-R26.question_text: What maneuver does bending your left arm straight upward at the elbow communicate?
sec11-card-sec11-R26.teaching_text: Raising forearm skyward makes your signal visible over the roof to cars trailing right behind.

sec11-card-sec11-R27.question_text: What does bending your left arm downward toward the pavement tell drivers behind you?
sec11-card-sec11-R27.teaching_text: Dropping your open hand downward warns following traffic before brake lights or engine braking slow you.

sec11-card-sec11-R28.question_text: What do right-of-way laws actually define, and what should you never insist on if crash danger looms?
sec11-card-sec11-R28.teaching_text: No statute grants anyone permission to plow into another vehicle just to prove legal priority.

sec11-card-sec11-R29.question_text: How must you approach a yield sign, and when may you proceed through?
sec11-card-sec11-R29.teaching_text: Treating yield signs as guaranteed roll-throughs cuts off cross traffic holding uninterrupted priority.

sec11-card-sec11-R30.question_text: To which approaching road users must a left-turning driver yield at an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-R30.teaching_text: Overlooking an oncoming bicycle while watching only sedans causes severe left-cross intersection injuries.

sec11-card-sec11-R31.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches running both siren and warning lights?
sec11-card-sec11-R31.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks fire trucks and ambulances from turning onto cross streets.

sec11-card-sec11-R32.question_text: Before pulling back into traffic after an ambulance or fire truck passes, what must you check for?
sec11-card-sec11-R32.teaching_text: Police cruisers and second fire engines frequently run seconds behind the lead siren unit.

sec11-card-sec11-R33.question_text: Where at intersections do lawfully crossing pedestrians hold right-of-way even without painted stripes?
sec11-card-sec11-R33.teaching_text: Sidewalk extensions form legal unmarked crosswalks at corners whether white zebra paint exists or not.

sec11-card-sec11-R34.question_text: Which mobility aids signal a blind or visually impaired pedestrian who holds absolute yield priority?
sec11-card-sec11-R34.teaching_text: Whether plain white or red-tipped, a cane or service harness requires full, patient driver yielding.

sec11-card-sec11-R35.question_text: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection, how must you treat vehicles already inside it?
sec11-card-sec11-R35.teaching_text: Letting vehicles already crossing clear the intersection box first prevents dangerous mid-junction T-bone collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-R36.question_text: At a T-junction without signals, who yields between drivers on the ending street and the through street?
sec11-card-sec11-R36.teaching_text: Drivers whose street dead-ends must turn, so uninterrupted through-road traffic holds natural priority.

sec11-card-sec11-R37.question_text: Who must yield when an unpaved dirt or gravel road meets a paved roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-R37.teaching_text: Paved highways carry faster through traffic, requiring drivers emerging off gravel or dirt to wait.

sec11-card-sec11-R38.question_text: What yield rule applies when pulling from parked curb space, an alley, a driveway, or the roadside?
sec11-card-sec11-R38.teaching_text: Entering live lanes from private drives or shoulders puts the full burden of finding a gap on you.

sec11-card-sec11-R39.question_text: When two vehicles stop at the exact same instant at a four-way stop, which driver yields?
sec11-card-sec11-R39.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right breaks simultaneous-arrival ties cleanly without hesitation.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Between what two distances from the nearest rail must you stop when a train warning or hazard is present?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet risks overhang impact, while stopping past fifty blocks queued sightlines.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: What action is mandatory when railroad crossing lights flash with an approaching train or a gate drops?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Trying to beat a dropping crossing arm gambles against freight momentum that takes a mile stopping.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Even without gates, when does a visible or horn-sounding train require you to stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Large locomotives look slower than they really move, creating immediate danger whenever horns sound.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Once you make a required railroad-crossing stop, when may you roll forward across the rails?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: On multi-track crossings, a second hidden train can arrive seconds after the first caboose clears.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Where inside a railroad crossing zone must your vehicle never come to a stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Even five seconds stationary across steel rails leaves you trapped if crossgates drop behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: When traffic ahead is queued beyond a railroad crossing, when is it safe to start across?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Entering behind slow bumper-to-bumper cars traps your rear bumper over the rails when traffic halts.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: If your car stalls on the tracks with a train coming, what should you do and which way do you run?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Moving away from the tracks toward the oncoming engine keeps flying wreckage from pelting you forward.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Which four actions does an advance railroad warning call for as you approach the tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Shedding speed early gives your eyes and ears time to catch trains at unguarded rural crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: Which two vehicle categories should you expect to stop at railroad tracks even when no train shows?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Tailgating a school bus or fuel tanker into a rail crossing triggers instant rear-end collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What letters and symbol make up railroad pavement markings, and what passing rule applies there?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Overtaking near tracks blocks your view of warning lights and risks head-on conflicts over rough rails.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How must a driver respond to a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: A crossbuck functions like a yield control for trains, requiring active speed drop and brake readiness.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What extra detail can a small plaque mounted beneath a railroad crossbuck warn you about?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Knowing multiple sets of rails lie ahead stops you from pulling out blindly behind a passing train.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Why must you look both ways at a crossing even when its red warning lamps stay dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Power loss or storm damage can silence electric flashers while a live freight train closes fast.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: How should a manual-transmission driver handle gear selection across railroad tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Missing a shift mid-crossing can stall the engine dead center across live steel rails.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: When crossing lamps begin flashing before the gate arm finishes dropping, what must you do?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Flashing red lamps carry the full legal stop command before the wooden arm ever reaches horizontal.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What is the rule on weaving around a lowered railroad gate, and when may you move?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Zigzagging around dropped arms is both unlawful and one of the deadliest gambles on highways.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: Why is assuming you know the local train schedule dangerous at familiar crossings?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Freight, maintenance, and rerouted trains run irregular hours that ignore everyday commuter habits.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: Why must you put away phones, headphones, and cabin distractions near railroad crossings?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: At wooded or angled crossings without gates, a locomotive horn may be your earliest warning.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: Which two pieces of critical data appear on a railroad crossing's emergency-notification plaque?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers that exact crossing ID lets them halt approaching trains on the right line immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Which two situations call for dialing the railroad crossing's emergency-notification number?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Alerting the railroad first stops oncoming trains when a car stalls or flashers malfunction.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: At a railroad crossing, how does a train's priority rank against cars, pedestrians, and even emergency vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Even ambulances running full sirens must wait for trains because steel wheels cannot swerve or brake short.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: May you back up on the travel lanes or shoulder of a controlled-access highway if you overshoot an exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Drivers pulling onto shoulders for emergencies never expect a car reversing toward them at highway closure speeds.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: Away from controlled-access highways, under what two conditions is backing a vehicle lawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Rear blind spots are huge on every car, putting full legal responsibility on the backing driver.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: When does carrying passengers or cargo violate Louisiana's safe-operation rule?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Stacked boxes hiding mirrors or crowded riders bumping your elbow cripple emergency steering and braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Which age group does Louisiana's guide bar from riding in an open pickup truck bed?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Open cargo beds have zero seat belts, turning hard braking or swerves into instant ejection hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Who may ride in an open pickup truck bed while traveling on an interstate highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: At interstate speeds, nobody of any age is allowed unrestrained in an open pickup bed.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: May passengers ride inside a house trailer while it is being towed along a Louisiana highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Towed house trailers lack crash-tested seating restraints and sway violently during sudden highway evasive maneuvers.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How must surrounding motorists treat vehicles traveling together in a funeral procession?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Cutting into a marked procession splits escorted family vehicles apart and creates chain-reaction confusion.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Which two light controls should drivers inside a funeral procession turn on?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Lit headlamps plus four-way flashers identify every car in the escorted line to cross-street drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How far back must you stay behind an emergency vehicle responding to a call?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Emergency rigs brake hard or U-turn into scenes suddenly, needing five hundred clear feet behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: What parking rule applies on the city block where an emergency vehicle stops to work a scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Sightseers parking inside the active block choke hose lines, stretchers, and incoming backup units.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: When is the only time you may drive across an unprotected fire hose stretched across pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Crushing a pressurized supply hose cuts water pressure instantaneously to firefighters working inside burning structures.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: What does Louisiana's guide ban over your ears while driving, and what medical exception exists?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Sealing off both ears blocks sirens, horns, and screeching tires that warn of blind-spot hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Which four dishonest or improper acts involving a driver's license are prohibited?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Altering dates, loaning cards, or lying on applications triggers criminal fraud and immediate credential penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How many valid driver's licenses may you hold, and what must you do if the department demands surrender?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Holding duplicate credentials across states hides violations, so law allows one card and mandates surrender.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Which three penalties does the guide warn can hit someone caught stealing motor fuel?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Driving off without paying for gas costs your driving privilege alongside criminal fines and potential lockup.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Which headlight setting is required whenever weather forces you to run your windshield wipers?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Daytime rain mist hides gray and silver cars unless low beams light both headlights and taillights.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: How must a bicyclist sit and grip the bicycle while riding on public roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Riding no-handed or standing off the saddle ruins emergency braking and instant obstacle steering.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: May a bicyclist grab onto or hitch a bicycle to a moving car or truck on a public street?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Skitching beside motor bumpers guarantees a violent fall the instant the car brakes or swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: Unless on a bicycle-only path, at most how many riders wide may bicyclists travel abreast?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Three or more riders wide blocks entire lanes and prevents safe three-foot overtaking passes.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: What defines a fictional-theft auto insurance fraud claim?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Stashing a car away to collect a payout commits insurance fraud that raises everybody's premiums.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: What repair-shop estimate trick does the guide describe as deductible-padding insurance fraud?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Offering to bury your deductible by padding insurer bills pulls vehicle owners into felony billing fraud.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: What dishonest shop shortcut makes up uncompleted-repair fraud?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: Leaving damaged structural parts unreplaced pockets insurer money and compromises crash safety next time.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: How can a deceptive insurance claim abuse old vehicle dents or prior collision damage?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: Filing old, already-settled dents under a fresh fender-bender counts as deceptive double-recovery fraud.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: Which three protections does the guide recommend when choosing a collision body shop?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Itemized written paperwork and backed parts-and-paint warranties protect you against hidden corner-cutting.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: Which everyday driving habit helps protect you from staged-crash scammers who slam their brakes?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: Fraud rings target tailgaters with sudden panic stops to manufacture rear-end injury claims.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: Right after a collision, whom should you call and what official record detail should you get?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: An official police report or item number locks in objective scene facts before stories change.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: What should you exchange after a crash, and what if the other driver refuses?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Letting the investigating officer step in avoids roadside arguments when another party hides details.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: Which two crucial facts can scene photographs lock in right after a collision?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Recording how many people actually rode in the other car blocks phantom-passenger injury claims later.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: Around which bystanders at a crash scene does the guide urge extra caution?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: Unsolicited strangers fishing for clinic or lawyer referrals at crash scenes often feed claim-fraud rings.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.question_text: How should you arrange a tow after a wreck, and what must be settled before hooking up?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.teaching_text: Bandit tow trucks can haul your car to high-fee storage yards unless you name the destination.

sec12-card-sec12-R25.question_text: What two follow-up steps protect your insurance claim once you leave the crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.teaching_text: Prompt reporting with your police item number lets adjusters spot exaggerated third-party claims early.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.question_text: Which three routine parking habits cut down vehicle-theft opportunities every day?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.teaching_text: Car thieves skip locked cabins under bright streetlamps in favor of dark, cracked-window targets.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.question_text: How should you store bags, electronics, or valuables when leaving your car parked?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.teaching_text: A visible backpack or laptop on a seat invites smash-and-grab glass damage in seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.question_text: During which three quick stops do drivers mistakenly leave keys in the ignition and invite theft?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.teaching_text: Opportunistic thieves watch gas pumps, convenience stores, and frosty driveways for idling unlocked cars.

sec12-card-sec12-R29.question_text: What does the guide say about stashing a backup key somewhere inside or under your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.teaching_text: Experienced car thieves routinely search magnetic wheel-well boxes, sun visors, and center consoles first.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.question_text: What security hardware does Louisiana's guide recommend adding to deter vehicle theft?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.teaching_text: Electronic engine immobilizers and visible locks stop hot-wiring and steer thieves away fast.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Why must you map out your interstate entrances and exits before leaving home?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Missing one rural interstate ramp can add many miles before the next interchange lets you turn back.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Which four vehicle items should you inspect before heading out on remote highways?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Lonely highway stretches offer few tow trucks or stations when low coolant or a flat spare strands you.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What traffic changes require attention while scanning ahead, behind, and beside you on the interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Scanning all four sides catches fast ramp entries and sudden brake waves before lanes compress around you.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Along with open following room ahead, what backup option should you always track in traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Knowing which open lane or shoulder sits free lets you steer clear instantly if brake lights lock ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What two steps come together whenever you enter an interstate highway?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Blinking early while sizing up an open pocket keeps right-lane traffic predictable during high-speed merges.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: When should you start checking mainline traffic as you enter an interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Waiting until the end of the ramp to look left steals time needed to match highway speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: How should you manage your speed while hunting a merge gap on an entrance ramp?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Entering close to mainline velocity prevents right-lane trucks from slamming brakes behind your bumper.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Between drivers already on the interstate and a driver entering from a ramp, who holds priority?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Ramp drivers join an established high-speed stream and must time their entry around mainline vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: What two things must a merging driver never assume about mainline motorists?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Adjacent cars may keep eyes forward or sit boxed in by left-lane traffic unable to slide over.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Should you stop before merging onto an interstate when open pavement allows rolling?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily at ramp's end forces a slow zero-speed launch into fast highway traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: When can driving slower than a posted interstate minimum speed become necessary?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Blinding rain, fog, or icy bridges override fair-weather speed floors whenever traction or visibility drops.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: How should you treat a freeway gap that looks barely long enough for your car?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Shoehorning between fast bumpers erases stopping cushions for both you and the driver behind.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Which three checks and signals come right before changing lanes for a merge?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Adding a brief side head check catches motorcycles or coupes hiding outside mirror glass.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What does the Louisiana guide advise regarding frequent, unneeded lane changes on the interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Every extra lane cross adds blindspot risk without meaningfully cutting arrival time.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: Which lane does the guide generally assign, and what three situations justify leaving it?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Keeping right frees outer lanes unless passing slower traffic, taking a left exit, or opening merge room.
sec13-card-sec13-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Stay right except pass, exit, merge

visual_sync.text_span: Stay right except pass, exit, merge

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: On an interstate with three or more lanes moving one way, how are the middle and far-left lanes used?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Cruising in the center lane keeps ramp merges clear on the right while leaving the far-left open to pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What upcoming traffic and driver adjustments does a highway merge warning sign signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Easing speed or sliding left early creates courteous breathing room before ramp traffic reaches the gore.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Which two sudden driver mistakes should you anticipate near interstate exits?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Distracted drivers realizing their ramp arrived late often stomp brakes or cut across lanes without warning.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Which four zones around your vehicle make up a complete highway space cushion?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Surrounding your car with open buffer zones gives time to brake smoothly or steer out of trouble.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Why should you avoid lingering right beside another vehicle on a multilane road?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Riding door-to-door sits you inside their blindspot and walls off your sideways escape lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: What front spacing rule still applies when another driver follows your rear bumper too closely?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Preserving extra forward margin lets you slow gradually for hazards so the tailgater behind can stop too.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Which three driver tools does the Louisiana guide name for managing space around your vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Adjusting pace, choosing smart lane placement, and signaling clearly work together to prevent squeeze plays.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: How should you read signs and move across multiple lanes ahead of your exit?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Stepping over one lane at a time with fresh mirror checks beats sweeping blindly across traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: Roughly how far before your interchange should you verify you are in the proper exit lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Lining up a full mile ahead spares you from fighting heavy truck clusters right at the ramp.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: When should your turn signal start blinking as you prepare to leave the interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Advance blinkers tell trailing traffic you are peeling off before your tires ever touch ramp paint.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What is the safe move if you miss your interstate exit, and what two moves are barred?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Stopping or backing along a fast interstate shoulder leaves closing traffic zero room to dodge rear-end collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: When an exit provides a deceleration lane, when should you slow down to the ramp's posted speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Getting all four tires clear of mainline lanes first keeps fast through traffic flowing smoothly.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What major traffic-direction shift must you watch for right after leaving a divided interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Hours on one-way divided pavement can trick drivers into turning into an opposing lane on local roads.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Why must your focus stay sharp on rural highways even when few other cars appear?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Empty country stretches lull drivers right before hidden tractors, livestock, or sharp ditches appear.
sec13-card-sec13-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Light rural traffic still demands focus

visual_sync.text_span: Light rural traffic still demands focus

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: What two adjustments belong on dirt or gravel roads, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Loose stones roll like marbles beneath tires, lengthening braking distance and kicking up blinding dust.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: Which two vehicle fundamentals suffer on rough, rippled, or potholed rural roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Bouncing tires skip across washboard ruts, weakening steering precision and lengthening stops.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: What three steps help you and nearby drivers stay safe inside swirling rural road dust?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Low beams cut through dust clouds so oncoming cars spot your nose before meeting head-on.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: What roadside features and oncoming pinch points make narrow rural roads hazardous?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Tiny shoulders drop straight into ditches, leaving scant room when wide oncoming trucks cross old bridges.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: What three precautions handle reduced traction across an open metal bridge deck?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Steel grating wanders slightly under tire grooves and turns slick fast whenever damp.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: How can roadside trees and tall farm crops create danger on country roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: High corn or brush walls off sightlines at unsigned country corners until cross traffic noses out.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: How must you approach a rural railroad crossing that has neither gates nor flashing lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: Without automated bells or arms, only your own eyes and slowed pace catch an approaching locomotive.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How should you approach an uncontrolled rural junction where no signs assign priority?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Country drivers sometimes roll familiar backroad corners fast, so easing in lets you yield safely.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Which four slow or vulnerable road users should you anticipate near hidden rural driveways and junctions?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Blind country lanes conceal pulling-out farm rigs, stopped buses, walking neighbors, and stray livestock.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: What does a posted deer-crossing sign tell drivers about the stretch ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Crossing diamonds mark habitual herd trails where sudden wildlife leaps happen year-round.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: During which two daily light transitions does wildlife movement spike near roadways?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Low sun angles and dim twilight hide gray deer coats right when animals feed along road shoulders.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Once you spot a single deer or animal beside the pavement, what should you immediately expect?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Herd animals follow the leader blindly across asphalt moments after the first one clears your hood.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: Where should your eyes scan when driving through signed or wooded wildlife zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Catching glowing eyes in roadside grass gives crucial braking distance before an animal bounds onto asphalt.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Which two panic steering moves must you avoid when an animal darts into your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Braking firmly in your lane beats hitting an oncoming truck head-on or rolling into roadside trees.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: Why must you drop speed whenever animals stand near the edge of the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Engine sound or headlights can spook calm grazing livestock straight across your front bumper.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Whom does the guide advise notifying after a crash with a large wild or farm animal?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Police clear dangerous carcasses off dark lanes and document damage for livestock owners and insurers.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: Below what speed does a vehicle travel when displaying a fluorescent orange-and-red slow-moving triangle?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Closing at fifty-five on a tractor rolling under twenty-five eats up following space in heartbeats.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How much roadway width can wide farm machinery take up on rural highways?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Combines and planters often overhang centerlines and narrow bridge rails at the same time.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: Why is passing a slowing tractor on the right risky when it swings slightly left?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Long towed implements need a wide left setup arc to clear tight right-hand field gates.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Why must you overtake slow farm equipment with extra caution instead of counting on sound?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Diesel roar and heavy implements keep operators from hearing your engine or horn behind them.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: What legal road right and rule duty apply to animal-drawn vehicles in Louisiana?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Horse-drawn wagons hold lawful roadway standing while following traffic duties alongside motor vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: How can stacked cargo on an animal-drawn wagon limit its driver?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Hay bales or bulky cargo hide trailing cars completely, so leave extra room before passing.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: Which two vehicle noises must you avoid when passing an animal-drawn wagon, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Startling a harnessed horse can send both animal and wagon lunging sideways into your lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: What turning moves should you anticipate when trailing an animal-drawn vehicle on rural roads?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Wagons lack bright electric blinkers and frequently turn into unmarked pasture gates or farm lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: How should you manage speed and lateral clearance when approaching a ridden or led horse?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: Giving riders wide, calm space keeps horses steady even if gravel pops beneath your tires.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: What noise rule applies near anyone riding or leading a horse beside the roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Sudden blasts beside a saddle horse risk throwing the rider onto hard pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: What should a slow-moving driver do when a line of delayed traffic builds behind?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Using a safe roadside turnout clears frustration before impatient drivers gamble on blind passes.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.question_text: Which two vehicle capabilities or parts suffer when you overload your car or truck?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.teaching_text: Excess weight overheats brakes on grades while bottoming springs and shocks through curves.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.question_text: Which three weight ratings must you check before hitching and towing a trailer?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.teaching_text: Staying inside trailer payload and gross combined vehicle limits keeps brakes and hitches safe.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.question_text: What two immediate adjustments belong whenever you hit heavy rain or fog?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.teaching_text: Slower speed protects wet traction while dipped beams light lane paint without bouncing glare back.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.question_text: When thick fog wipes out safe forward vision, what beats creeping slowly along the highway?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.teaching_text: Crawling half-blind in a live lane invites high-speed rear-end chain collisions from behind.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.question_text: In which five traffic or weather situations does the guide call for low-beam headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.teaching_text: Low beams spare nearby mirrors from glare while cutting cleanly underneath falling rain, snow, or mist.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.question_text: What optical problem happens if you flip on high beams inside fog or precipitation?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.teaching_text: Airborne droplets act like tiny mirrors that throw high-beam light right back into your eyes.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.question_text: What two visual and lighting mistakes must you avoid when facing bright oncoming headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.teaching_text: Staring into brights bleaches night vision, and flashing high beams back blinds the oncoming driver too.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.question_text: Why must sunglasses and tinted lenses come off for nighttime driving?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.teaching_text: Darkened glass blocks scarce street light needed to spot dark pedestrians and unlit shoulder hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.question_text: What distance rule caps your safe travel speed after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.teaching_text: Driving faster than your beams reach guarantees hitting unseen obstacles before your brakes can finish stopping.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.question_text: At least how many seconds of following room does the guide recommend on rural roads at night?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.teaching_text: Stretching your night cushion to four seconds offsets slower hazard spotting on unlit country asphalt.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.question_text: How does the guide distinguish an open driving zone from a closed driving zone?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.teaching_text: Tagging blocked lanes or blind crests as closed zones prompts early speed or lane adjustments.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.question_text: Which five roadway and traffic elements can shift quickly as driving conditions change?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.teaching_text: Work zones, storms, or rush hour shrink lanes and visibility together, demanding constant re-evaluation.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.question_text: How does lowering your speed on crowded urban streets help hazard handling?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.teaching_text: Crosswalk walkers, opening doors, and delivery vans crowd city blocks, so slower pace buys thinking room.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.question_text: How can combining errands or carpooling lower your overall crash risk?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.teaching_text: Every eliminated solo errand cuts miles spent mingling with traffic congestion and distracted drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.question_text: Which six route and roadside details belong in smart pre-trip route planning?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.teaching_text: Checking route numbers, fuel stops, rest breaks, and work detours ahead keeps your eyes off maps mid-drive.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.question_text: Which seven mechanical and visibility parts should you inspect before starting a road trip?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.teaching_text: Spotting cracked belts, worn hoses, or low brake fluid in the driveway prevents highway tow bills.

sec13-card-sec13-R37.question_text: Which four reference items and backup funds belong onboard for unexpected road-trip needs?
sec13-card-sec13-R37.teaching_text: Paper maps and emergency money rescue trips whenever rural cell towers or card readers go down.

sec13-card-sec13-R38.question_text: What simple spare item does the guide advise carrying on trips against loss or accidental lockouts?
sec13-card-sec13-R38.teaching_text: Keeping a spare fob or key tucked separately turns a rest-stop lockout into a ten-second fix.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: While no prep removes every road danger, what skill helps a driver respond in time?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Spotting trouble developing blocks ahead turns panic emergencies into calm speed or lane adjustments.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Which four path, cockpit, restraint, and cabin tasks belong before pulling out?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Clearing cabin clutter and dialing seat and mirrors while parked keeps your full attention forward.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How do visual, manual, and cognitive distractions each pull a driver off task?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Losing sight, grip, or mental focus separately already hurts control, and combining them multiplies danger.
sec14-card-sec14-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Eyes away, hands busy, mind elsewhere

visual_sync.text_span: Eyes away, hands busy, mind elsewhere

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Why does texting behind the wheel rank among the worst driving distractions?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Reading and typing steal your eyes, hand, and brain simultaneously across football-field highway distances.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Besides phones, which five routine cabin habits does the guide list as driver distractions?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, checking mirrors to groom, or tapping touchscreens steals crucial hazard-scanning beats.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Even with both hands on the wheel, which type of distraction can a hands-free device still cause?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Deep phone conversations shrink visual scanning and slow braking reactions even without touching glass.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What phone step before shifting out of park cuts the urge to check alerts mid-drive?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Muting chimes before rolling stops notification buzzes from pulling your eyes toward the console.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What two safe options handle a call that genuinely cannot wait during a trip?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Pulling into a lot or handing phone duty to a rider keeps your eyes locked on traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: When should you review directions for an unfamiliar destination instead of reading them on the move?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Knowing upcoming turn names beforehand stops panicked glances down at turn-by-turn screens in intersections.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: How should you manage pets before leaving and handle a child needing help during a drive?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Twisting into the backseat while rolling sends cars drifting across centerlines or shoulders in moments.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: What is the rule when your phone, drink, or sunglasses slide onto the floorboard while moving?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Groping beneath pedals pulls your head below dash level and tugs the steering wheel off line.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Into which four broad categories does the guide group factors that contribute to collisions?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Seeing how car faults, road layout, surface wear, and human choices interact sharpens defensive scanning.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Which three mechanical vehicle systems can contribute directly to a crash when neglected?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Every evasive stop or swerve relies on healthy rubber, hydraulic brakes, and tight steering linkage.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: Which three roadway maintenance or work-zone conditions create sudden collision hazards?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Scanning far ahead spots dropped cargo, deep ruts, and lane shifts early enough to steer smoothly.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: Which four driver behaviors does the guide spotlight as prime collision hazards?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Crowding bumpers, cutting lanes, rushing, and forcing right-of-way erase everyone's margin for error.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Where should heavy or loose cargo ride whenever possible, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Unsecured laptops, tools, or coolers fly forward at highway speed during sudden braking or impact.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Which three groups of items belong inside a prepared driver's collision kit?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Having paper, pen, coverage cards, and warning gear together keeps post-crash steps calm and organized.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Why check your owner's manual before an emergency stop ever tests your brakes?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Knowing beforehand whether anti-lock brakes are installed prevents pumping pedals meant for firm steady hold.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How do anti-lock brakes help a driver during an emergency stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Keeping tires rolling instead of skidding lets you steer around the obstacle while braking firmly.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: What does an ABS dashboard warning lamp tell you when it stays lit after startup?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: A glowing fault lamp means anti-lock pulsing may be offline right when slick pavement arrives.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: If an oncoming car drifts into your lane, which escape direction must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Swinging left meets the drifting driver head-on the instant they wake up and jerk right.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Why does the guide require buckling your lap-and-shoulder belt on every single trip?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Even flawless defensive drivers face sudden red-light runners where seatbelts decide survival.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: How can a sideways-sliding vehicle end up rolling over?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Digging sideways rims into soft shoulder turf or concrete curbs flips momentum over the roof.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: How does a higher center of gravity change a vehicle's rollover behavior?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Tall SUVs, pickups, and vans lean harder in sharp swerves than low-slung sedans.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Which two driver inputs commonly trigger vehicle rollovers?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Whipping the wheel hard at high speed throws weight sideways faster than tires stay planted.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: How should you recover if your tires drop off the edge of the paved roadway?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Snapping the wheel hard against a pavement lip launches the car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: What deadly rollover outcome do fastened safety belts help prevent?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Being thrown through glass into rolling steel accounts for huge shares of fatal rollover injuries.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: How do modern side airbag systems help shield riders when a vehicle tips?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Tilt sensors trigger side curtains across window glass to cushion heads and help block ejection.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What happens when you turn sharply or brake abruptly on wet or icy pavement?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Harsh pedal or wheel spikes exceed low wet grip instantly and break the tires loose.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: When the rear of your vehicle slides sideways, how should you steer?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Cranking too far whips the tail violently the opposite way into a secondary fishtail.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Why might two different vehicles react differently to braking and steering inputs?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Front-wheel, rear-wheel, all-wheel, and electronic stability setups each handle traction shifts uniquely.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: During traction loss, how should you steer and where should you aim your eyes?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Your hands naturally follow your gaze, so looking down your open lane beats staring at ditches.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: How does electronic stability control detect a slide and help keep the vehicle straight?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Pulsing one corner's brake nudges a sliding nose or tail back onto your steered line automatically.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What three rules govern steering, brakes, and throttle when your tires hydroplane on water?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas smoothly lets speed drop until tread sinks back onto solid asphalt.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: What is your top priority if your car stalls on railroad tracks with a train approaching?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: No vehicle is worth a life when a freight train needs over a mile to stop.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: At the instant a tire blows out, what must you do with the wheel and brake pedal?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Stomping brakes on a shredded tire pitches weight onto the bad corner and spins you out.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Once a vehicle with a blown tire slows under control, how do you finish stopping?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Coasting down first lets gentle pedal pressure ease you off live lanes without rim spinouts.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: If your accelerator sticks open, where do your eyes stay and what gear do you select?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Neutral disconnects runaway engine power from the wheels while keeping power steering and brakes alive.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: What critical mistake must you avoid while stopping a vehicle with a stuck accelerator?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Turning the key fully off while rolling can lock the steering column straight toward a crash.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Why must you avoid yanking or stomping the parking brake abruptly if main service brakes fail?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Locking rear cables abruptly spins the tail around when you have no hydraulic front brakes.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Once a vehicle with failed brakes finally stops, may you limp it home slowly?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Rolling even one block without working brakes puts every crosswalk and intersection at lethal risk.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What trouble does steam billowing from under the hood signal, and what two steps come first?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Continuing to run a boiling engine warps cylinder heads and bursts pressurized coolant hoses.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Why must your hands stay off a radiator cap right after an engine overheats?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Pressurized boiling coolant erupts upward instantly if unlatched before the block cools down.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: What four-step sequence handles smoke coming from beneath your hood?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Under-hood smoke warns of electrical or fuel fire that can flash into the cabin fast.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: Should a driver try battling a large vehicle fire personally?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Burning tires, fuel tanks, and airbag canisters explode unpredictably beyond pocket-extinguisher reach.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: Why are cigarettes, matches, and open flames banned around a vehicle battery?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: One stray spark near hydrogen battery vapor can shatter the acid casing in your face.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: At the very first sign your car is failing, how should you use remaining momentum?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Gliding onto a wide shoulder early beats stalling dead inside a center travel lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What two traffic habits still apply while steering a failing vehicle out of its lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Panic swerving across adjacent lanes without signaling trades a breakdown for a high-speed sideswipe.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Once parked safely off the road, how do you warn approaching motorists?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Bright blinkers and roadside triangles alert distracted drivers long before they drift toward the shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: Where around a broken-down roadside vehicle must you never stand?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Passing cars clipped onto shoulders crush anyone standing at the trunk or lane-side door.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: If your disabled car cannot clear a live travel lane, where should occupants stay while help arrives?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Sitting inside a dead car blocking live highway speed leaves occupants helpless against rear impacts.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: When your disabled car sits well clear of traffic, what does the guide advise doing?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Staying locked inside away from asphalt protects you from both passing traffic and strangers while calling.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: Should you stand roadside trying to wave down passing traffic for breakdown help?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Flagging fast traffic causes sudden brake-checks and puts you inches from moving mirrors.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: Why can vehicle exhaust poison cabin occupants without them noticing a scent?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Because deadly carbon monoxide carries no odor, headaches or sleepiness hit before anyone smells fumes.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: Which two common situations let dangerous carbon monoxide build up around occupants?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Cracked tailpipes under the floor or idling inside a shut garage concentrates lethal gas fast.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: What immediate action does the guide direct if anyone suspects exhaust-gas poisoning?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Stepping outside into clean oxygen right away stops rising carbon monoxide levels before unconsciousness.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: What must you do whenever floodwater covers the roadway ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Moving flood currents sweep heavy SUVs off bridges in far shallower water than drivers guess.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: Why can even shallow-looking floodwater over a road still wreck or trap your vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Storm runoff often carves deep sinkholes or missing culverts invisible beneath muddy surface water.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: If floodwater blocks your path and no detour exists, where should you go?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Parking up on high ground keeps rising flash-flood water clear until levels drop safely.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: If your vehicle plunges into deep water, when must occupants start escaping?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Power windows and cabin buoyancy last brief moments before rising water traps doors shut.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: What three survival steps in order does the guide's water-escape cue POGO stand for?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Unbuckling first, dropping side glass before electronics short, and climbing out beats fighting flooded doors.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: After any crash causing injury, death, or property damage, what must you do instead of driving off?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Fleeing a collision turns an ordinary traffic accident into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.question_text: Which two emergency services should you summon after a crash when injuries may exist?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.teaching_text: Getting officers and paramedics rolling immediately secures the scene and treats hidden trauma.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.question_text: Whose names and details should you gather at the scene of a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.teaching_text: Independent witnesses leave quickly, so jotting their names early preserves neutral crash accounts.

sec14-card-sec14-R30.question_text: Which details must crash-involved drivers exchange, and what card must be presented on request?
sec14-card-sec14-R30.teaching_text: Sharing accurate contact, registration, and driver-license proof satisfies your legal post-crash duty.

sec14-card-sec14-R31.question_text: What three duties apply if you strike an unattended parked car or roadside property?
sec14-card-sec14-R31.teaching_text: Leaving clear contact details while alerting police prevents an unattended scrape from becoming hit-and-run.

sec14-card-sec14-R32.question_text: Which six travel, occupant, timestamp, and weather facts should you write down after a collision?
sec14-card-sec14-R32.teaching_text: Recording exact lanes, directions, passenger counts, and sky conditions stops memory drift weeks later.

sec14-card-sec14-R33.question_text: How soon after a traffic collision should you notify your insurance company?
sec14-card-sec14-R33.teaching_text: Prompt reporting protects policy coverage and starts claim handling while repair and witness facts stay fresh.

sec14-card-sec14-R34.question_text: When is moving an injured person after a collision justified?
sec14-card-sec14-R34.teaching_text: Shifting someone with hidden neck or spine trauma risks permanent paralysis unless fire or traffic threatens life.

sec14-card-sec14-R35.question_text: Which four steps secure a vehicle before you walk away and leave it unattended?
sec14-card-sec14-R35.teaching_text: Setting the parking brake and pocketing the key prevents runaway rollaways and opportunistic theft.
sec14-card-sec14-R35.must_match_memory_hook: Stop engine, lock ignition, key, brake

visual_sync.text_span: Stop engine, lock ignition, key, brake

sec14-card-sec14-R36.question_text: What three actions are required when an authorized emergency vehicle approaches using warning signals?
sec14-card-sec14-R36.teaching_text: Clearing promptly to the right curb gives fast-moving rescue rigs an unobstructed lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R37.question_text: On a multilane highway approaching a stopped emergency vehicle, when do you change into a nonadjacent lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R37.teaching_text: Checking mirrors before vacating the adjacent lane protects roadside responders without sideswiping traffic beside you.

sec14-card-sec14-R38.question_text: What must you do passing a stopped emergency vehicle when changing lanes is unsafe or impossible?
sec14-card-sec14-R38.teaching_text: Slowing way down gives you tight braking control right beside officers working feet from your mirror.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Under Louisiana law, how serious is driving while impaired by alcohol or certain drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Driving impaired goes far beyond a simple traffic ticket and carries serious criminal prosecution.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Is alcohol pharmacologically classified as a stimulant or as a depressant?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Even when social drinks feel lively at first, alcohol slows central-nervous-system signaling needed to drive.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Which four core driving abilities suffer after consuming alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Losing sharp eyes, alertness, sound choices, and quick footwork leaves zero defense against sudden traffic stops.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Why do people sometimes feel energized right after drinking even though alcohol is a depressant?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Dropping mental brakes feels like excitement while coordination and hazard reaction are quietly slipping.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: Does switching between beer, wine, and liquor change impairment, or what truly governs the effect?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Standard pours of beer, wine, and spirits deliver comparable pure alcohol into your bloodstream.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: Which two drinking and meal factors change how quickly alcohol enters the bloodstream?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Drinking fast on an empty stomach spikes blood concentration far quicker than pacing with food.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: Can hot coffee, working out, or a cold shower sober up an impaired driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: A wide-awake impaired person still carries the exact same blood alcohol slowing eyes and reflexes.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What is the sole factor that clears alcohol out of the body?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Your liver processes alcohol at a steady pace that no shortcut or home remedy speeds up.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Which three spatial judgments needed in traffic get distorted by alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed, following gaps, or corner angles turns routine merges and turns into crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: How does drinking change a driver's sense of caution toward traffic laws?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Blunted caution tempts impaired motorists into speeding, tailgating, or running red lights they soberly respect.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What everyday vehicle controls can an alcohol-impaired driver forget to use when concentration drops?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Tunnel attention makes impaired drivers cruise dark streets unlit or turn abruptly without signaling.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: Which two fundamental traffic maneuvers suffer from alcohol-slowed driver responses?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Reacting half a beat late at a red light or corner carries your bumper straight into cross traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: Why should someone who has been drinking never trust their own sense of fitness to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Alcohol dulls the very self-awareness brain circuits needed to recognize slurred reflexes.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: Which two alertness and eyesight problems can alcohol trigger behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Heavy eyelids paired with out-of-focus lane lines push cars across centerlines and onto shoulders.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: What duty applies if someone you know has been drinking asks to drive the vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Keeping keys away from an impaired friend protects them and everyone sharing the road tonight.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What measurement does blood alcohol concentration describe?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Measuring alcohol inside a set volume of blood gives courts an objective impairment benchmark.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: How can officers estimate a driver's alcohol concentration without drawing blood?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Deep-lung breath carries alcohol in direct proportion to bloodstream levels, allowing fast roadside testing without needles.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What BAC threshold does the Louisiana guide state for noncommercial drivers aged twenty-one or older?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Reaching point zero eight triggers adult per-se DWI regardless of how steady someone claims to feel.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: What lower BAC threshold applies to Louisiana drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Underage drivers cross point zero two quickly from roughly one drink and face immediate consequences.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to begin affecting your ability to operate a vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Subtle focus and eye-tracking shifts begin well below per-se legal limits right after drink one.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: Which four erratic lane or speed patterns warn that another driver ahead may be impaired?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Recognizing lane drift, jerky stops, or abnormal creeping early lets you hang way back out of range.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Which two in-vehicle alcohol actions does the Louisiana guide restrict?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Keeping unsealed bottles or cans inside the cabin brings legal trouble even before anyone fails a breath check.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: What two broad consequences follow a DWI conviction under the guide?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: A single conviction stacks fines or jail exposure atop losing your legal right to drive.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: How should you position your car around a driver who looks intoxicated instead of intervening?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Trying to box in an erratic driver invites a high-speed collision with someone unable to react.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Should you flash lights or motion at a suspected impaired driver to pull over?
